News.title: More areas of UK likely to move into drought as fifth heatwave builds
News.content:
Sunday is forecast to be a warmer day across many areas with temperatures widely getting up to the mid to high twenties Celsius. South-east England will be even hotter where temperatures could rise as high as 33C.

After a cooler day on Monday, temperatures will then rise widely across the UK from Tuesday.

In Scotland and Northern Ireland, temperatures will typically reach the low to mid twenties.

In England and Wales, temperatures will rise into the mid to high twenties Celsius and widely across east Wales, central, eastern and southern England in excess of 30C.

The heat is set to peak on Thursday, with readings of 35C possible in south-east England.

If this happens, it will be the fourth consecutive month of 35C or more being recorded.

The threshold for declaring an official heatwave is likely to be reached widely across England and Wales, making it the fifth heatwave of the year for many.

Yellow heat health alerts are in effect for most of England until 21:00 BST on Tuesday, warning of impacts for health and social care services and an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

These are likely to be updated in the coming days as heatwave conditions develop.

News.title: Andy Burnham to embark on cost of living tour through the UK
News.content:
The prime minister is set to announce "a series of measures to make life easier" for those struggling with the cost of living in the coming days, Downing Street says.

No 10 says Andy Burnham's plans are to "give people some room to breathe". He will also focus on ways of "improving high streets" as he embarks on a tour of the UK.

But the government is facing continued pressure over its early release scheme for prisoners in England and Wales â with criticism of the fact that two of PC Andrew Harper's killers will be eligible from next year.

Burnham is also likely to face pressure for more action on the cost of living â although significant interventions are unlikely before October's Budget.

Even then, Chancellor John Healey has made it clear he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" â which will limit how much the government has to spend.

The prime minister has been on holiday this week, but Downing Street said he would be in "listening mode" in the coming days as he tours the UK's nations and regions and works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

A spokesman for the prime minister said: "He thinks Westminster has got used to telling people that everyday hassles â like hidden pricing and consumers being ripped off â must be accepted as part of life.

"He doesn't think that's right. That's why he's going to start rolling out a series of pro-consumer cost of living measures to give people some room to breathe."

The spokesman added: "He's also going to be kicking off his summer tour around the country, getting out of Westminster and meeting people where they are.

"The prime minister is going to be in listening mode to help inform his 10-year plan to bring back hope and make Britain better off."

There are, though, likely to be continued questions about the forthcoming early release scheme, due to start in October.

One of Burnham's first acts in Downing Street was to order a review which limited the range of people who would be eligible.

But those convicted of manslaughter will still qualify for the scheme â including two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper.

The prime minister has faced calls from PC Harper's family, former senior police officers and opposition politicians for them to be denied early release.

But he has said he cannot go any further without risking prison capacity. Downing Street said on Saturday night that position remained unchanged, despite reports the prime minister could revisit the case.

News.title: Killed a month after his wedding - why PC Andrew Harper's story touched so many
News.content:
On the night of 15 August 2019, Lissie Harper got a knock at the door. She thought it was her husband Andrew coming home from work.

Instead, it was uniformed officers, there to tell her that the man she had married four weeks earlier had been killed while on police duty.

"Everything I had known in my life to be true was robbed away. Every ounce of beautiful peace, gone," Lissie later said of the moment she was told.

They had met as teenagers and were together for 13 years.

In her eulogy at his funeral, Lissie recalled how Andrew would pass her notes in class.

They were, she said, "true childhood sweethearts, loving one another more and more with each passing day".

They had been about to go on their honeymoon.

But, on that night nearly seven years ago, everything changed.

The case has been back in the headlines because two of PC Harper's killers â Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole â will become eligible to be released early under government plans to tackle prison overcrowding.

As the disturbing details of the case are revisited, his family, fellow officers and the public are outraged once more â at what happened, and at the perpetrators' impending release.

PC Harper's death was brutal and devastating, causing shock, anger and an outpouring of grief across the country.

Pictures of the smiling faces of his teenage killers laughing and joking as they left court only added to that anger.

PC Harper had been about to head home at the end of a long shift when he and a colleague were called to reports of a burglary.

He was "going beyond the call of duty", the prosecutor at the Old Bailey trial in 2020 said.

During the case, haunting dashcam footage from the police patrol car was played showing the moment PC Harper confronted teenagers Henry Long, Bowers and Cole down a dark country lane. He then disappeared from view.

His ankles had got caught in a strap trailing behind the car being driven by Long that had been used to tow a stolen quad bike.

PC Harper was dragged for over a mile. He died on the road. His police badge and stab vest were found scattered along the route.

The three teenagers were tried for murder. In the end, the jury convicted Bowers and Cole of manslaughter. Long had already pleaded guilty to that offence.

It meant the jury was not sure that PC Harper's killers knew they were dragging the officer behind the car.

But the Judge, Mr Justice Edis, described it as a manslaughter case which was "very close to a case of murder" in its seriousness.

News.title: How weight-loss medication is changing relationships with alcohol
News.content:
There is a growing body of research into the link between weight-loss drugs and alcohol consumption.

The drugs, with brands including Wegovy, Mounjaro and Ozempic, contain semaglutide or tirzepatide, which mimic a natural hormone called GLP-1. This suppresses appetite and keeps people feeling fuller for longer, helping them to lose weight.

Early research suggests that because these drugs affect the reward response in the brain, they can reduce cravings for substances including alcohol and nicotine, says Dr Christian Hendershot of the University of South Carolina.

He published a small-scale study, external in 2025 in which participants with alcohol use disorder craved alcohol less while taking Ozempic. Alcohol use disorder, sometimes referred to as alcoholism, is described by the NHS as drinking in a way that is harmful.

A study, external from the University of Colorado Anschutz published last week also suggested that GLP-1 medications in pill form led to fewer days of heavy drinking in people with mild to moderate alcohol use disorder.

People taking the drugs told BBC News that alcohol had affected them in different ways: some said their cravings for it had gone, drinking had made them feel nauseous or uncomfortably full, or they had got drunk more quickly. Others said they had not noticed any effect on their relationship with alcohol.

Before she started taking Wegovy, Lisa says she drank between six and eight bottles of wine a week with friends. But she had sometimes worried about whether this was too much and whether it could damage her health.

NHS guidance, external is that people should not drink more than 14 units a week on a regular basis, which is about six medium glasses of wine or six pints. Drinking too much in the long term can lead to liver damage, high blood pressure and increased risk of cancer.

Lisa says that since starting on the medication she has more than halved her consumption. At a recent day festival, she drank three glasses of wine over the course of nine hours. Previously, she would have had two bottles plus a couple of vodka mixers, she says.

Alcohol has always been a big part of her social life and when she stopped drinking for a few weeks in the late 2010s, she realised friends had stopped inviting her to social events. It led her to start drinking again.

This time round, Lisa says that she still looks forward to drinking wine, but after having a couple of glasses she simply cannot stomach any more.

"I still feel involved in things because I'm still drinking but drinking a lot less," Lisa says.

For years, Warren Thomas, 45, from Colchester, had enjoyed an occasional beer with his family after work, as well as one or two heavy drinking sessions with his friends each month.

But when he spoke to his friends on weight-loss medication about his plans to start taking Mounjaro, they warned him that it could affect how much he drank.

Warren says he noticed the effect within 24 hours of his first dose in mid-June. "I just don't want to drink," he says. "I've just got no appetite for it."

When he went out for his friend's birthday last month, he felt "light-headed and a little bit giddy" after two beers, he says.

"My tolerance level to drinking is now zero," he says.

There is no formal advice in the British National Formulary, a guide to dispensing medicine used by doctors and pharmacists, about whether people on weight-loss drugs should stop drinking alcohol, says Prof Russell Hearn, a GP and professor of medicine at King's College London.

But he gives careful advice to his patients. "Alcohol has a lot of calories in it and if your goal is to lose weight, drinking less will definitely help you with that alongside changing your diet while you're on a GLP-1," he says.

For people like Lisa and Warren, drinking less alcohol has been a happy bonus. But recent graduate Faye Goodwin, 20, feels that it has hampered her social life.

When Faye drinks she says she gets nauseous very quickly and sometimes throws up or gets bad acid reflux.

Faye, who got in touch with BBC Your Voice, has been taking Mounjaro since she was 18 and does not really know what it is like to drink alcohol without the impact of weight-loss medication. But she says she once took a month off the jabs and was able to drink without experiencing any nausea.

News.title: Australia is the planet's extinction hotspot, but one animal offers a glimmer of hope
News.content:
"Eyes peeled," comes the order from the front passenger seat.

Obediently, we scan the ends and tops of logs, looking between low scrub and patches of vivid wildflowers for a flash of stripes or a dart of movement.

Eluding us is the numbat, a rare Australian marsupial which could be the love-child of a chipmunk and an anteater.

Numbats were once populous across the bottom half of the continent, but Dryandra Woodland â in the south-western corner of Australia â is one of the few places they remain.

As we slowly roll along bush tracks, researchers explain how this annual trip helps plot the species' survival.

Classified as endangered until this month, numbats have been bouncing back. This team's efforts have seen them scratched off the international red list of threatened species - a rare glimmer of hope in a country facing an extinction emergency.

This part of Australia is the front line of that crisis: a last stand for many species driven to the brink by feral pests, disease, urban development, habitat destruction and climate change.

Winging over our car at one point is the endangered Carnaby's cockatoo. On an island just off the coast is one of the last surviving pockets of the world's rarest marsupial, the Gilbert's potoroo. Diving in the sapphire waters around it is the increasingly scarce Australian sea lion.

News.title: Zendaya saw me on the red carpet and her jaw dropped - I'm still in shock
News.content:
"I can't zip this! Mummm?"

This was 29-year-old Zainab Jiwa, calling out for help squeezing into a corset while filming a "get-ready-with-me" TikTok video. It's a scene many 20-somethings still living at home will relate to.

The difference is, Zainab was on her way to the recent London premiere of The Odyssey, one of the summer's biggest blockbusters.

She was invited there as a guest and says she caught the eye of Hollywood megastar Zendaya, thanks to her custom look: a striking gold gown complete with a hood.

"She just walked past, and she saw me there. Her jaw just dropped, so did mine," Zainab tells me.

"It was just a stare-off for a minute, and she was like, 'Oh my god, amazing, amazing,' and then she just walked off."

"Iâm still in shock,â she adds. âThe thought of her noticing my outfit blew my mind."

The interaction went viral, external with 19m TikTok views. Her phone blew up.

While Zendaya has been ruling the red carpets with high-fashion "method dressing" â where stars match outfits to a film's themes â Zainab is perhaps proving that independent creators like her can give Hollywood a run for its money.

Zainab, who is Muslim and wears a hijab, is also often one of the only people covering her hair at premieres, but she says finding ways to incorporate modest wear is part of the fun.

"Even though you're covered, you can still find a way to be on theme.â

News.title: Why eclipse chasers are crossing continents for solar spectacle: 'It's like the World Cup'
News.content:
On Wednesday, parts of Europe will be plunged into daytime darkness as the moon passes in front of the sun, temporarily blocking its light and casting a shadow across the continent.

For many of us, it will be a once-in-a-lifetime experience. But for some, following eclipses has become something of an addiction.

Armed with two high-spec cameras, a specialist telescope and a drone, Mark Griffiths has spent two days driving from Cheshire to Galicia - one of the best places to view the eclipse - to record the event.

It's a hobby that started six years ago, when he went to Shetland to see the northern lights - though the weather was so dreary he "didn't see anything".

But it didn't put him off and he soon found he couldn't stop. He loved the thrill of witnessing and capturing the sky's most spectacular events.

News.title: Hundreds arrested over French wildfires, but who is to blame?
News.content:
After wildfires caused more damage in France this year than at any time since World War Two, many are left asking a single question: why?

A major driver is that climate is changing as a result of the well-documented way humanity is burning fossil fuels. Temperatures are only rising.

But with records showing that nine out of 10 French wildfires are started by humans, the government in Paris is trying to attribute blame - although it is itself accused of being underprepared for the infernos that have now scorched more than 300,000 acres this summer.

The interior ministry has announced 420 arrests of people alleged to have either started the fires deliberately or by accident. Among them are 166 minors.

In one case, a 23-year-old man has been accused of deliberately starting 10 fires in the space of five days in the south-eastern Var area last month. He faces 15 years in prison and a â¬150,000 (Â£128,000) fine, if convicted.

Many others have been tried and immediately sentenced, such as a man who received a three-year jail sentence for starting three recent fires in the Raon-L'Ãtape forest in the Vosges region.

"Only a few square metres of vegetation went up in smoke," noted L'Est RÃ©publicain, the newspaper that reported the story.

Other prosecutions have been perceived as heavy-handed and unjust. A homeless man and someone with severe autism have reportedly been handed jail terms for throwing cigarette butts.

"I was amazed at the number of arrests, it feels excessive," admits Muriel Gestas, a lawyer who has represented several people accused of arson, including two firefighters. She doubts many will lead to a conviction.

The newspaper Le Monde is also unconvinced. It questions to what extent police have examined these cases, given the short time frame.

The authorities' silence on the details - the specific charges, notably whether they involve intent and how the numbers compare with past seasons - rules out any meaningful comparison with previous years, it argues.

But Bordeaux prosecutor Renaud Gaudeul told Le Monde that a tough approach was justified by current circumstances.

"The conditions for a charge of endangering lives are met for those who throw a cigarette butt or light a barbecue in wooded areas. It only takes a tiny spark for it to start," the newspaper quoted him as saying.

News.title: Family 'devastated' as hit-and-run driver who killed boy, 13, to have early prison release
News.content:
The family of a 13-year-old boy killed in a hit-and-run say they are "devastated" after being told the driver who caused his death has had his sentence reduced.

Kaylan Hippsley died three days after being struck by a car driven by Harley Whiteman on Brecon Road in Hirwaun, Rhondda Cynon Taf, on 29 February 2024.

Whiteman was originally sentenced to six years and nine months in prison and banned from driving for eight years and four months but, after Kaylan's family appealed, High Court judges increased the sentence to nine years.

Now, the family has been told Whiteman can be released under licence as early as this autumn as part of the UK government's Sentencing Act early release scheme.

News.title: Kellie Bright to leave EastEnders after 13 years
News.content:
EastEnders star Kellie Bright is to leave the soap after playing one of its key characters, Linda Carter, for 13 years.

She arrived in Albert Square with on-screen husband Mick, portrayed by Danny Dyer, when they became the new owners of the Queen Vic pub.

Carter's matriarch character has been central to major storylines including plots about murder, sexual assault and alcoholism.

Bright said she made the "tough decision" to leave more than a year ago but "happily" agreed to stay on to be part of an "exciting storyline".

The BBC has promised "unmissable drama" before her on-screen exit, which is said to be a "while away" yet.

Executive producer Ben Wadey described the actor as being "the beating heart of EastEnders" and said she had become "a classic EastEnders icon".

Viewers have seen the much-loved character at the heart of many emotional storylines including in 2014 when she was raped by her brother-in-law Dean Wicks.

More than 7 million people watched the episode which prompted dozens of complaints. The sexual assault led to long-running story arc about family conflict and trauma.

News.title: Rare turtle to be sent back home in 5,000-mile 'incredibly emotional' trip
News.content:
It has taken almost two years to plan, including building a special temperature-controlled crate for him, and co-ordinating complex paperwork across two countries.

Rhossi normally lives in the sea, but has to travel out of the water â first by helicopter from Anglesey to London, then by cargo flight to Houston, Texas, USA.

It means the journey needs to be completed as quickly as possible, and staff have to be constantly on hand to make sure he does not dry out or dehydrate.

Davidson said: "We have to make sure that the shell is really well lubricated, so we spread Vaseline all over to stop it drying out and flaking off.

"The same for the skin â it's really delicate â and especially the eyes, which both have to be lubricated before he goes into the crate and again just before takeoff, or he will start to peel like someone getting sunburned.

"But I have had to go to the checkout in a chemist's with about eight tubes of KY Jelly and three tubs of Vaseline and explain what's happening when I get strange looks."

News.title: Hot weather reveals hidden history across the South
News.content:
As the south of England continues to enjoy an unusually warm and dry summer, parch marks on lawns across the region have revealed the hidden histories of their location.

Among the sites which have seen the outlines of historic installations exposed by the hot weather are Portchester Castle and Blenheim Palace.

At Blenheim, the footprint of an 18th century garden - which had once stretched across the width of the entire palace - has revealed itself on a lawn.

Andy Mills, the Unesco World Heritage Site's head gardener, told the BBC it was "absolutely magical" to see the outlines of the historic parterre - 260 years after it was demolished.

Mills explained that the original parterre - which is a French word meaning 'on the ground' - had been constructed in 1705, and would have "cost an absolute fortune to install".

"It was a very large extravagant thing to do, but it was a way of showing your wealth and importance and that sort of thing," he said.

News.title: Attempted murder arrest after three hit by car
News.content:
A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and dangerous driving after three pedestrians were hit by a car following reports of a disturbance.

The incident happened on Stokes Croft in Bristol at about 06:30 BST, according to Avon and Somerset Police.

A spokesperson for the force said one of the pedestrians was taken to hospital, but their injuries were not considered to be life-changing or life-threatening. The two others were not seriously injured.

A man police believe to be the car's driver was treated for facial injuries after his arrest.

Thomas Street, Hepburn Road, Stokes Croft and City Road are all closed while police make enquiries, with more officers than usual in the area as investigations continue.

The Best Off Licence in Stokes Croft was also damaged in the incident.

Bristol Supt Matt Ebbs said: "We would like to assure the public we do not believe there to be any wider threat.

"Anybody with concerns is welcome to speak to officers on the ground, but we would also appeal to anybody with CCTV, dashcam or mobile phone footage which may assist our enquiries to contact us."

News.title: Banksy works cost public almost £150,000
News.content:
Three artworks by street artist Banksy have cost taxpayers almost Â£150,000 in cleaning operations and security so far, with the bill expected to rise.

The largest single cost relates to a mural painted on the Royal Courts of Justice in September 2025, where removal efforts and security have so far cost more than Â£85,000.

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) says it has spent Â£50,000 trying to remove paint from the wall of the Grade II-listed building in Carey Street. A further Â£35,300 was spent on overtime and security costs.

The spending was disclosed to the BBC through Freedom of Information requests and is likely to reignite debate over whether Banksy's work is vandalism or valuable public art.

Banksy, who emerged from Bristol's graffiti scene in the 1990s and became one of the world's most famous street artists, is known for murals and installations that often appear overnight and attract large crowds.

The latest costs relate to a mural depicting a judge in a wig battering a protester with his gavel, which appeared on the Royal Courts of Justice in London on 8 September 2025.

Banksy claimed the image as his own work, by posting it on his website and Instagram account.

News.title: Stray cats showing up at raves, gigs and pubs now have own merchandise
News.content:
Celebs pulling in punters with a club appearance is nothing new. But did they ever have so much fur?

At venues in Coventry at least, the glitterati wear whiskers these days.

It began when two stray cats made city venues their home, becoming social media stars thanks to the incongruous sights of tail and turntable, pint and paw.

While one shows up at gigs and rave nights, the other is a bit more pub than dub. But each now has his own range of merch... and visitors flock for a glimpse of these meeow-vers and shakers.

Murphy was first spotted living beneath a bush before wandering into the car park of The Old Windmill pub in the city centre, "rake thin" and in need of care.

Now a permanent resident, he has become a firm favourite with customers.

"We've had people who've never been in the pub before, but have seen him on social media," said the venue's Peter Dunkley. "They come in and the first question is 'where's Murphy'?"

Across town, Fargo is a well-known figure at Fargo Village, the creative hub after which he is named.

Regularly spotted around the site's shops and bars, he too has become an attraction in his own right, mixing among ravers and drinkers.

Fargo Village staff have set up an Instagram account in an effort to track down his owner, and it has attracted a loyal following of fans eager to keep up with his daily adventures.

News.title: Man's body found in burning car
News.content:
The body of a man has been found inside a burning car in Portadown, County Armagh.

Police were called to the scene at Harford Street in the town centre at about 22:00 BST on Saturday.

Firefighters extinguished the blaze and the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Ch Insp Tierney, from the Police Service of Northern Ireland said the circumstances are under investigation and a post-mortem examination will be carried out to determine the cause of his death.

The cause of the car fire will also be investigated.

The vehicle's windows were smashed and it was significantly damaged by the blaze.

A neighbouring property in the street sustained scorch damage, according to police.

The officer added: "Ammunition Technical Officers (ATO) were also tasked to the scene to conduct relevant enquiries â we can confirm there is no risk to the public."

News.title: Liverpool vs Monaco LIVE: Reds surrender two-goal lead again in pre-season friendly at Anfield
News.content:
Why Andoni Iraola Is PERFECT For Liverpool

Andoni Iraola will manage Liverpool at Anfield for the first time as his side welcomes Monaco for their penultimate friendly of pre-season.

Liverpool experienced mixed fortunes in their tour of the United States, which saw them beat Sunderland and Wrexham before enduring a dismal capitulation against Leeds in their final outing, surrendering a two-goal lead in the second half to lose 4-2 to their Premier League rivals.

Iraola will hope to take key lessons from that match into his Anfield bow against the Ligue 1 side, two weeks out from their season opener at Newcastle.

The Spaniard now has almost his full squad at his disposal after the likes of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson Becker and Cody Gakpo returned from their post-World Cup breaks, while new signing Victor Munoz could also be in line for a debut.

Federal officials have issued a recall alert for meat products containing jalapeños due to potential salmonella contamination.

A recent salmonella outbreak linked to the peppers has affected at least 345 people across 27 states, predominantly in Minnesota and Colorado. No deaths have been reported, but 36 individuals required hospitalization.

The FSIS said Saturday August 8 that customers across the U.S. should check their fridges and freezers for red meat and poultry products containing jalapeños, because they may also be contaminated with salmonella.

It released a list of 18 recalled products affected by the alert, with brands including Taylor Farms, Ready Meals, Meal Simple, Higher Harvest and Deli Kitchen.

Products include Deli Kitchen’s Chipotle Cheddar Chicken Wrap and Cajun Chicken Mashed Potatoes & Corn stocked at Kroger/Dillons, with use-by dates ranging from 08/07/2026 to 8/13/2026.

open image in gallery Salmonella outbreak has been linked to jalapeño peppers grown in Sinaloa, Mexico ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

The affected Taylor Farms products include its Classic Beef Burrito, Chipotle Chicken Wrap, Chicken Verde Burrito and Chicken Enchilada sold at Hannaford and Kroger. Use-by dates on the products range between 08/07/2026 to 8/16/2026. You can find the full list here.

The agency said in a statement that it “expects additional downstream products will be identified as this ingredient recall progresses.”

The first illnesses in the salmonella outbreak were reported in June, and were linked to jalapeño peppers grown in Sinaloa, Mexico. The peppers are distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors to wholesalers, restaurants and food service companies, according to the FDA.

The USDA said that so far “there have been no confirmed reports of illness” from products regulated by FSIS that contain jalapeños that were sourced from Sinaloa.

Data compiled by the CDC found that of 191 patients who were interviewed about their illness, 93 percent reported eating at a Mexican-style restaurant before falling sick, including popular chains Chipotle and Qdoba.

open image in gallery Chipotle announced this week that it had pulled jalapeños from some of its restaurants due to the ongoing salmonella outbreak ( Getty )

Chipotle announced this week that it had pulled jalapeños from some of its restaurants, and Qdoba did the same shortly after.

“Given their actions to remove product from their stores, neither of these establishments are considered a current ongoing risk to consumers in this outbreak,” CDC officials said in a statement.

The FDA is investigating whether any of the jalapeños went to grocery stores. The agency may announce additional actions on its recalls webpage, health officials said.

On August 8, grocery store chain Albertsons announced that it was voluntarily recalling four items containing jalapeño products, including salsa and corn salad, supplied by Taylor Farms.

Symptoms for salmonella can include diarrhea, fever and stomach cramps. The illness usually lasts four to seven days, and most people recover without treatment.

Young children, elderly adults and people with weakened immune systems are at higher risk for more severe illness, according to the CDC.

President Donald Trump spent his Saturday evening on Truth Social, releasing a series of seemingly AI-generated posts mocking up the planned White House ballroom and its rooftop “drone port.”

In three different images all titled “DronePort”, the president depicted the roof of the ballroom structure covered by numerous military drone aircraft, armed soldiers and refueling trucks, turning the placid grounds of the White House into a major military installation. The images were the same ones he originally posted in May, as he attacked a federal judge for delaying the project by ruling that the administration lacked congressional authorization.

“This great and very important military asset sits atop the heavily protected Ballroom at the White House. It provides National Security for Washington, D.C., and will protect future Presidents!!!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

The president’s focus on his ballroom is not new. His fixation on the military center and “drone port” pictured in the three images he released late Saturday evening comes, however, as he has shifted his rhetoric about the construction project to focus on its planned security features in an attempt to win further congressional support for funding and battle a court order stopping construction. Money for the ballroom was originally set to be approved by Congress as part of legislation passed earlier this year, but it was stripped out due to lack of support in the Senate.

Like his first post back in May, this latest posting by the president follows his defeat in court over the project.

open image in gallery Donald Trump disembarks Air Force One in New Jersey on 7 August. The president continues to insist a deal is coming with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz ( Reuters )

open image in gallery One of three AI-generated images depicting the planned White House "drone port" ( The White House )

A federal appeals court delivered the second blow to the project on Friday that the administration must cease construction of the project until congressional approval is gained, leaving the building process in limbo and putting another awkward test to the Republican-controlled House and Senate with just a few months to go before the midterm elections.

The president frequently veers off onto tangents about the ballroom and its construction process during unrelated events and planned remarks as the project (and the totality of his D.C. beautification efforts) have become a clear, sustained priority that at time often trumps matters that would seemingly be more important to Republican voters, to say nothing of the officials and dignitaries often in the room listening to him wander off topic and derail his own speeches.

His efforts to beautify D.C. include projects to restore fountains and other park features around the District of Columbia as well as the now heavily scrutinized effort to restore the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, fixing leaks in the structure’s base and repainting the surface with an aqua-blue swimming pool coating.

open image in gallery Construction of the White House ballroom and ‘drone port’ remains in limbo after an appeals court ruled it must be halted ( Reuters )

open image in gallery The Reflecting Pool is once again closed to the public as efforts to properly resurface it continue ( Reuters )

That project has also consumed his attention in recent days as his U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, Jeanine Pirro, dropped charges against an Olympian falsely accused by the Trump administration of vandalizing the pool’s new coating with a knife or other sharp object. Pirro admitted in court filings that the damage to the coating appeared to be the result of a faulty installation process.

Apart from the chunks of pool coating that were visible in the waters as the new surface failed, the waters of the pool turned lime-green this summer as park workers struggled to deal with a massive algae bloom which the president also previously attempted to blame on vandalism. Like the failed installation of the coating, the algae was actually thought to be the result of contractor error during the addition of new micro-bubbler devices to the structure.

The president has pivoted to describing the ballroom and “drone port” project as an issue of national security as his popularity and subsequently the appeal of his D.C. renovation projects has waned on Capitol Hill. On Friday, he attacked the appeals court that ruled against his adminsistration in court on the project for supposedly endangering the lives of current and future occupants of the White House, with his rationale being that the planned structure’s anti-drone capabilities were the only thing that could guard from such attacks.

“The Circuit Court’s decision, which is totally wrong on the vital subject of STANDING, of which the plaintiff has none, severely jeopardizes the lives and welfare of the people who work, and will be working, at the White House — including all future Presidents of the United States, and their families, as well as the lives of all those visiting,” wrote Trump.

News.title: Faithful dog leads best friend’s funeral procession
News.content:
A 15-year-old collie-spaniel cross named Bo led the funeral procession for his owner, Graham Price, 74, who was laid to rest in South Wales on Tuesday, August 4.

Price shared an unbreakable bond with Bo, whom he had owned since the dog was a puppy.

For more than 20 years, Price played bass guitar with Crazy Cavan ’n’ the Rhythm Rockers, a Welsh rockabilly band closely associated with the Teddy Boy movement.

Formed in 1970, the band built an international following and continued touring and recording until the death of its frontman, Cavan Grogan, in 2020.

News.title: Burnham to tour UK asking people how he should tackle cost of living and stop people being ripped off
News.content:

Andy Burnham is set to launch a national tour this week, seeking public input on how the government can improve their lives.

Officials confirmed he will be in “listening mode” throughout August, travelling the country to discuss the cost of living.

Having promised “breathing space”, Mr Burnham is expected to unveil new measures to help with bills.

Mr Burnham said on his first day in office that he did not want to end his time as prime minister without taking the difficult decisions needed to tackle England’s social care crisis, which he said had bedevilled governments for almost three decades.

Mr Burnham said on his first day in office that he did not want to end his time as prime minister without taking the difficult decisions needed to tackle England’s social care crisis ( Kirsty Wigglesworth / AFP via Getty Images )

He has also begun his tenure in Downing Street with a series of measures aimed at easing financial pressure on families, including cutting VAT on energy bills, reducing business rates for pubs, clubs and music venues, and capping bus fares at £2.

However, the Conservatives have challenged Mr Burnham to explain how he plans to fund the pledges, questioning where the money for his various commitments will come from.

The upcoming tour will also see Mr Burnham focus on improving high streets. Officials stated this summer engagement will inform his 10-year plan for the country.

A spokesperson for the prime minister added he would be “getting out of Westminster and meeting people where they are”.

They added: “He thinks Westminster has got used to telling people that everyday hassles – like hidden pricing and consumers being ripped off – must be accepted as part of life.

“He doesn’t think that’s right. That’s why he’s going to start rolling out a series of pro-consumer cost-of-living measures to give people some room to breathe.”

With the fallout from the Iran war keeping inflation higher than expected, the cost of living remains a major concern among the public.

A poll published by Ipsos at the end of July found 30 per cent of people listed the economy as a major concern while 22 per cent listed inflation or prices specifically.

But opposition figures have accused Mr Burnham of “tinkering” with his announcements.

Reform UK’s economic spokesman Robert Jenrick said the prime minister should “scrap green levies and taxes on energy bills”, and rule out tax rises in October’s budget.

He added: “It’s high time the Labour Party cut the ballooning benefits bill so we can relieve pressure on the hardworking majority that hold our country together.”

News.title: This is a grave wrong that has been allowed to fester for too long
News.content:

Even in the midst of an unprecedented prisons crisis there are still people incarcerated with an effective life sentence that they did not deserve.

Many should have been released long ago.

Now Dame Vera Baird, chair of the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC) has told The Independent of her deep concerns about these continuing injustices, and why people imprisoned under the discredited Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) regime need to have their plight examined much more quickly.

Speaking out for the first time since Andy Burnham ordered an investigation into this scandal, Dame Vera calls for “wholesale” action to review or resentence those involved.

This would be in the interests of both individual justice and in creating space in the cells such that early release can be avoided for far more dangerous criminals.

It is no exaggeration to say that two of the notorious killers of PC Andrew Harper now slated for early release would not now be in the brink of undeserved freedom had the IPP disgrace been ended.

At the moment, the understaffed CCRC is trying to cope with an increasing number of IPP cases, with more than 180 already under review - which is still a small proportion of the 2,400 or so still outstanding.

Reflecting on this intolerable situation Dame Vera asks: “Who could expect that it would last this long and cause so much damage, which I'm afraid it has done…It's very odd that we're left over with a lot of people are still stuck on something that we all accept should never have been implemented.”

Dame Vera’s dedication to the cause is sincere, and her public intervention an unusual and necessary one, but official redress is, as she points out, is long overdue.

This is a mass injustice that has been allowed to fester for an inordinate length of time, and caused, fundamentally, by political complacency born out of public indifference.

This is of course all too true of the criminal justice system more generally. There are always more popular ways to invest public money than in building costly new prisons and paying lawyers to process cases, so it should come as no surprise when the system collapses, as it is doing now.

Although the Conservatives have an especial responsibility for the neglect of more recent times, few ministers have shown much enthusiasm for the challenge to “make prions work”; but they have always readily agreed to calls for longer, harsher sentencing to prove they are “tough on crime”.

Retribution has taken precedence over rehabilitation and economy. It was always absurd that judges should have been able to lock people up indefinitely for any sort of offence, let alone relatively minor ones, simply for an unprovable suspicion that the individual was dangerous.

The IPP provision broke the link that made a punishment for the crime. The terrible consequences of this mistake have been felt ever since.

The IPP regime has destroyed lives needlessly. It was brought in during the Blair administration, when Dame Vera was a Labour MP, and even then sceptical about its usefulness.

A typical IPP case would be of a young man, say in their late teens, jailed in the 2000s, but, perhaps with some periods of failed probation, still serving time for an offence that should have been punished with a determinate sentence, as was the case before and since the disastrous IPP experiment.

If they were sent to prison at the age of 19, say, they have now lost the best years of their lives, and to no great benefit to public safety.

It has taken public outrage and yet another collapse in the prison system to impel a prime minister into acting, but the IPP review ordered by Andy Burnham is no less welcome for that.

The modest investment in the extra resources that Dame Vera and the CCRC need to finish the job swiftly would be repaid many times over.

News.title: Late own goal secures draw for Chelsea against Johor in feisty friendly
News.content:
Johor 3 Chelsea 3

Chelsea ended their Far East tour with a hard-earned draw against Malaysian champions Johor.

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight, it was also no shock to see the Malaysian powerhouses offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

The hosts had the better of the match and thanks to goals from Arif Aiman, Oscar Arribas and Bergson held a 3-2 lead with two minutes left of the 90.

The visitors, however, had one last attack and Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That came after two penalties from Liam Delap in a match that saw tempers overflow in each half.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Sports.title: ‘It’s in the contract!’ – Chelsea penalty shootout chaos erupts as pre-season friendly hit by farcical row after draw
Sports.content:
CHELSEA avoided humiliation amid farcical scenes at the end of their far-flung Far East tour.

An incident-packed, bad-tempered game ended level on the scoresheet and with 11 players still on both teams.

A late own goal by Johor Darul Ta’zim prevented the Blues losing in normal time and a penalty shootout was expected to settle the winners.

But it never happened.





A member of the Chelsea backroom staff was overheard saying “it’s in the contract” to the referee.

Yet both teams and staff left the field, never to return.

Sports.title: Chelsea 3 Johor 3: Xabi Alonso set for sleepless night with second-string Blues WOEFUL against Malaysian minnows
Sports.content:
CHELSEA avoided humiliation amid farcical scenes at the end of their far-flung Far East tour.

An incident-packed, bad-tempered game ended level on the scoresheet and with 11 players still on both teams.



A late own goal by Johor Darul Ta’zim prevented the Blues losing in normal time and a penalty shootout was expected to settle the winners.

But it never happened.



A member of the Chelsea backroom staff was overheard saying “it’s in the contract” to the referee.

Yet both teams and staff left the field, never to return.

Xabi Alonso’s side were ragged for much of the game and deserved to fall behind in the first half.

Then two penalties from Liam Delap put the Blues in the driving seat, only for JDT to equalise and then move ahead with five minutes to go.

Delap flicked on a cross from substitute Mykhailo Mudryk to force Antonio Glauder into an own goal.

But then an entertaining evening was denied more drama when the shootout was called off and the Blues were left to head back to Europe.



Defeat would have been a real embarrassment for Chelsea, despite extenuating circumstances.

Yes, it was a mainly second string side which took the field only 15 hours after the squad touched down at 4am local time in Jakarta.

Yes, it was still 30C and humid as anything.

And JDT have won the last 12 Malaysian titles in a row.

But still there are no excuses for a Premier League team losing to such opposition.



And Chelsea should have been three down at half time yet could have been 2-1 up.

After a good start going forward, worries about the team out of position in the 3-4-2-1 formation were proved well founded.

It was far too easy for JDT to break and Marcos Guilherme outpaced Tosin Adarabioyo before crossing to the back post, where captain Arif Aiman fired home.

Aaron Anselmino should probably have done better but the Argentinian was soon forced off with injury, after Mamadou Sarr had also been a late withdrawal from the starting line-up.

The Blues were soon all over the place.



Jamie Gittens was struggling as a left wing-back and Oscar Arribas wasted a brilliant chance to make it 2-0.

JDT also fluffed yet another good break and were punished immediately.

Delap’s strength led Kevin Medina into a silly foul which conceded a penalty.

Delap scored emphatically but then showed the other side to his game.

First, the £30m signing from last summer was needlessly booked for getting involved in a scuffle with an opponent.



Then Delap was played through by Nicolas Jackson’s brilliant pass in first-half stoppage time but sent a first-time shot wide.

If Alonso’s message at the break was to tighten up at the back, no-one listened.

Shahab Zahedi ran clear for JDT but allowed half-time substitute goalkeeper Gaga Slonina to make a good save.

Chelsea continued to look open at the back, but on the hour they went ahead.

Gittens did something right at last, winning a softish penalty.



Once more, Delap was decisive from the spot.

But JDT were soon level. Arribas’s free kick took a wicked deflection off Delap’s back and it was no more than the home team deserved.

The needle in the game returned when Antonio Glauder went through the back of Delap.

Tosin led the brawl on the pitch, while set-piece coach Austin McPhee was involved in a scuffle between the two benches.

Clear-cut chances had dried up until Dario Essugo’s poor pass allowed JDT sub Bergson to put his side 3-2 up with five minutes to go.



But Alonso’s double change paid dividends immediately.

Sub Mudryk swung in a cross, Delap got a faint touch and the ball took a big deflection off Glauder to level the score.

And so to penalties.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Or not.

More to follow…

Sports.title: Chelsea hit by DOUBLE defensive blow as Xabi Alonso’s plans take a major injury hit in pre-season
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S new manager Xabi Alonso has been dealt a double injury blow ahead of the new season.

Alonso, 44, has been tasked with bringing the Blues back on their feet after a chaotic season that saw three managerial changes and a tenth-place finish.



However, the Spanish tactician has endured a turbulent pre-season that has seen him dealing with a bloated squad and two friendly losses to rivals Tottenham and Juventus.

And now the ex-Real Madrid boss saw two defenders limp off during the West Londoners’ penultimate friendly against Johor Darul Ta’zim.



Mamadou Sarr pulled out injured just before kick-off after being named in Chelsea’s starting line-up.

And Aaron Anselmino was then forced off injured midway in the first half played in Malaysia.



Neither Sarr, 20, nor Anselmino, 21, have been key players for the Premier League giants.

The defensive pair were also not being primed for Chelsea’s first team ahead of the 2026/27 season.

Sarr joined the Blues from Strasbourg in 2025 but was immediately sent back to the sister club on loan until this past February when he came back to Stamford bridge.

The centre-back currently counts a mere total of six appearances with the West Londoners.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Anselmino, on the other hand, joined Chelsea in 2024 from Boca Juniors but was loaned back to the Argentinean giants before undergoing some more short stints at Borussia Dortmund and Strasbourg.

The centre-back has only managed one appearance across all competitions with the Prem outfit in which he only played three minutes.

Alonso already has a raft of options to choose from at centre-half, which includes the likes of Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Tosin Adarabioyo, Josh Acheampong and summer signing Maxence Lacroix.

Benoit Badiashile, Trevoh Chalobah and Axel Disasi are also still in Chelsea’s books but look set to move away during the summer transfer window.

Sports.title: Man Utd working on stunning transfer for teen superstar Louis Page ‘with Arsenal also keen on Leicester ace’
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED are trying to sign Leicester City teenager Louis Page.

Page only turned 18 last month but has already made 17 appearances in the Championship.



Leicester are now in League One and United are working on a deal for midfielder Page as part of a new signing strategy.

Sources say United have also held dialogue about a possible move for another talent who is younger than Page.



According to BBC Sport, Arsenal are also keeping an eye on Page, as well as Aston Villa.

United are looking to add more youth talent to their ranks after buying 18-year-old winger Tynan Thompson from Tottenham in a deal rising to £8million last month.

That deal was similar to when United signed Ayden Heaven from Arsenal in the 2025 winter transfer window.

Heaven was also 18 at the time and had made only one senior appearance for the Gunners.

He made his United debut a month after joining the club and overall made six appearances in the 2024-25 run-in.

Page came on in the 79th minute of Leicester’s League Cup win against Northampton Town on Saturday and Leicester start their League One campaign at Notts County on Saturday.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Thompson was signed on the promise of eventual first-team integration.

He has already trained under head coach Michael Carrick.

Sekou Kone was also 18 when United signed the Mali international in August 2024.

Kone has just rejoined the Ineos-owned FC Lausanne Sport for a second loan spell.



Should Page arrive, he will become United’s seventh arrival of the summer.

Carrick has already brought in Karl Darlow, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Kit Margetson, Cristian Oroczo and Thompson.

The Red Devils have also been liked with the likes of Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall and Fulham defender Antonee Robinson.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford arrives at Carrington as England star jets to Man Utd pre-season after being left without squad number
Sports.content:
MARCUS RASHFORD was among seven players who travelled to the Republic of Ireland to link up with Manchester United teammates for their training camp.

Rashford reported to United’s Carrington training complex early on Sunday morning and flew to Dublin at 11am.



The 28-year-old pulled up in a white Audi before signing autographs and posing for pictures.

United played Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on Saturday and flew straight to Ireland, where they are staying at Carton House in Maynooth.



The club arranged for a private jet to ferry Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Karl Darlow, Benjamin Sesko, Senne Lammens, Matheus Cunha and Matthijs de Ligt across the Irish Sea.

Rashford and Mainoo have now completed their mandatory three-week post-World Cup breaks after England and Argentina participated in the third-place play off and final last month.

Sesko has missed all four pre-season friendlies so far as he continues his recovery from a shin injury while Lammens and Cunha were absent for the 1-1 draw with PSG due to illness.

De Ligt has been out since November with a back injury and underwent surgery in May that will cause him to miss the start of the season.

Rashford has not played for United since he was substituted in their 2-1 Europa League win at Viktoria Plzen in December 2024.

The 28-year-old has not trained with teammates since January 2025 as he has spent spells on loan at Aston Villa and then Barcelona.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Barca passed on a £26million option to buy Rashford while Villa signed Alejandro Garnacho, Rashford’s former left-wing competitor, on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy from Chelsea.

Rashford is United’s highest earner on £325,000 a week and has two years left on his contract. The club privately remain open to selling him.

United have also scrapped plans for an open training session at Carton House amid suspicions that Rashford’s presence has influenced the change in plans.

Amazon will also be sending a crew to film United’s stay in Ireland as cameras start rolling on the All or Nothing documentary that will chart the club’s upcoming season.



Rashford does not have a squad number at United after Cunha received the ‘10’ last year.

Arsenal and Tottenham are both in the market for a winger and sources close to Rashford have welcomed links to the Premier League clubs, though it is unclear if either side will move for the England international.

United coach Michael Carrick clammed up when asked about Rashford by Norwegian broadcasters VG after United played PSG.

Carrick noted he and Rashford have “history” as Carrick was the captain when Rashford made his United debut against Midtjylland in February 2016.

United play Leeds at Croke Park on Wednesday but Rashford is likelier to get a run-out against AC Milan in Wroclaw on Saturday.

Sports.title: Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links
Sports.content:
Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links

Former Manchester United striker Michael Owen has cast doubt on whether Benjamin Sesko is the right long-term centre forward for the club

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko has been linked with a Manchester United exit this summer (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Michael Owen has explained why he has “doubts” that Benjamin Sesko could be a long-term option for Manchester United. Sesko signed for the Red Devils last summer from RB Leipzig in a deal believed to be worth around £74million.

‌



There have been reports in recent weeks providing speculation around Sesko’s future at United, with the striker scoring 12 goals during his first season at Old Trafford.

‌



Sesko was granted more minutes for United after Michael Carrick took charge at the start of the year, but did not feature in any of the final four matches of the campaign with a shin injury.

‌



Sesko's future has been a subject of discussion over the summer, with reports in recent days suggesting that Bayern Munich are considering making an approach for the United striker. Sesko is said to be viewed by Bayern as a possible long-term replacement for Harry Kane.

"Whether they push [Matheus] Cunha up front or [Bryan] Mbeumo or whoever, they've managed without him.

Sports.title: Arsenal respond to Gabriel Martinelli transfer approach as Mikel Arteta lays out demands
Sports.content:
Arsenal have received an approach from Galatasaray regarding a possible move for Gabriel Martinelli. However, the Gunners are not expected to consider the Turkish club's advances unless a replacement is lined up.

The Mirror's sister-title football.london report that the 25-year-old is currently in Mikel Arteta's plans but the ambitious move for Vinicius Junior indicated a desire to strengthen out wide with other clubs taking note of Martinelli's potential availability.

Christos Tzolis has already joined this summer and has been Arteta's chosen left winger throughout pre-season. The former Norwich City man scored in the win over Girona and assisted Piero Hincapie's headed goal in the defeat to Real Betis.

Arsenal's champion squad will leave Mikel Arteta having to digest harsh reality READ MORE :

A desire for more consistent output appears to be the reason behind Arsenal's pursuit of another attacker with Martinelli managing just one Premier League goal across 30 outings last season.

‌



He produced an impressive Champions League campaign during the league phase, but failed to find the net in any knockout fixture en route to the final.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

That impact when it matters seems to be what Arsenal are looking for. Should they identify a suitable option, it would likely trigger a change in approach regarding Martinelli's situation.

The player is thought to be content in north London and retains aspirations of competing at the highest level, but the guarantee of consistent game time and the prospect of being displaced by another new signing could alter that outlook.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is looking at more Arsenal new signings

Arteta addressed the media following the clash in Girona, hinting that further transfer activity could be on the horizon over the coming weeks. Bruno Guimaraes has already been confirmed as an Arsenal signing, though additional deals are still anticipated.

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously," the Spaniard added, speaking after a 4-1 pre-season victory over Girona.

"We want to get better like anybody else, and you just can see the transfer market and our opponents, what ‌we are doing. We won't sit still, and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

‌



"The margins are very small. Because we want to get better, and the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we ‌don't have in the team."

Sports.title: Mason Mount injury latest as Man Utd sweat on star after pre-season blow
Sports.content:
Mason Mount injury latest as Man Utd sweat on star after pre-season blow

Mason Mount has impressed in pre-season but he gave Manchester United a scare by picking up an injury just 20 minutes into Saturday's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain

View 2 Images Mason Mount came off injured against Paris Saint-Germain (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been given a boost after learning that Mason Mount's injury is not serious. The United midfielder came off after just 20 minutes during Saturday's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



It left Michael Carrick sweating on the fitness of Mount, 27, with less than two weeks to go until the Red Devils start their Premier League season away to newly promoted Hull City. But the midfielder left the stadium in Gothenburg, Sweden walking freely, suggesting that his pre-season wasn't over.

‌



Mount has now flown to Ireland ahead of United's next training camp in County Kildare. He'll be joined by Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez, who were each given additional time off following the World Cup.

‌



Having only started two of Carrick's 17 games in charge last season, Mount has given a good account of himself in pre-season. Playing in a deeper role, the former Chelsea star has put together an encouraging run of performances.

United have been intent on signing a third midfielder throughout the transfer window, but Mount's displays could prompt them to shelve their plans and focus on recruiting for other areas. Left-back is a position which the Red Devils want to strengthen before deadline day on Tuesday, September 1.

Mount's resurgence has also seen ex-United winger Lee Sharpe label him captain material. The 27-year-old currently isn't part of United's leadership group.

Sports.title: Liverpool given Ronald Araujo transfer update as Hansi Flick makes Barcelona admission
Sports.content:
Liverpool given Ronald Araujo transfer update as Hansi Flick makes Barcelona admission

Ronald Araujo is set to complete his move to Liverpool after the Reds agreed to sign the Barcelona captain on a season-long loan deal with an option to buy

View 2 Images Ronald Araujo of Barcelona is expected to join Liverpool on loan (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has confirmed that Ronald Araujo will complete a move to Liverpool. The Reds have been linked with signing a new central defender following the injury to Joe Gomez during pre-season.

‌



News emerged earlier this week that Liverpool had agreed a deal to sign Araujo from Barcelona on a season-long loan, which will also include an option to make the move permanent.

‌



Gomez’s injury has left Liverpool with only one fully-fit senior centre-back in their squad (Virgil van Dijk), while Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni are still recovering from their injury concerns.

‌



Araujo has arrived on to Merseyside on Sunday to undergo a medical to become a Liverpool player.

The 27-year-old has spent the last eight years at Barcelona, racking up 213 appearances and netting 14 goals, and was named as the club's captain in January following the loan exit of Marc-Andre ter Stegen.

Darwin Nunez has given thumbs up to Liverpool transfer as deal gets seal of approval READ MORE :

However, he managed only 16 starts last season and took time away for mental health reasons after facing severe criticism following his red card during the Champions League defeat to Chelsea in November.

‌



Araujo came back in January and lifted the La Liga trophy in May after Barcelona defeated fierce rivals Real Madrid 2-0 at the Camp Nou to secure first place.

However, Flick is allowing his skipper to depart and speaking following his side's friendlies against Nottingham Forest and Udinese on Saturday, he said: "I think Ronald is a great guy and a fantastic player.

"I think our style of play, that we want to play, is a little bit different. He's a player that has a lot of speed, he's physical and very strong and also with the ball he's quite good.

‌



View 2 Images Ronald Araujo is set to join Liverpool on loan from Barcelona. (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We couldn't include him like I wanted and also I think he wants to make something new. You know it more than me because in the past, something has happened, so this affected him.

‌



"I saw him this morning and I said goodbye and I think he was very happy and Liverpool is also a fantastic club. I wish him all the best because he deserves it.

"He's a fantastic guy and fantastic player and was a great captain."

It's understood the season-long loan features a £47m option for Liverpool to sign rather than an obligation.

‌



The Reds are grappling with several defensive absences as they continue preparations for their Premier League curtain-raiser at Newcastle United on August 23.

At centre-back, Gomez faces several weeks out with a muscle problem sustained in the friendly against Sunderland; new arrival Jacquet is yet to appear as he regains fitness following shoulder surgery; Leoni remains absent from an ACL injury suffered last September, and teenager Ifeanyi Ndukwe is ineligible.

At right-back, Conor Bradley has been unavailable since January following a serious knee injury while Jeremie Frimpong has been dealing with several fitness problems since his move from Bayer Leverkusen last summer. Liverpool host Monaco at Anfield at 2.30pm on Sunday.

Sports.content:
PSG move could hand Marcus Rashford last-gasp Man Utd transfer with Barcelona reunion

Marcus Rashford is expected to stay at Manchester United but a Paris Saint-Germain transfer approach could open the door to a permanent Barcelona move

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford could have been handed a Barcelona transfer chance by Ferran Torres (Image: (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images))

Ferran Torres looks to have handed Marcus Rashford a chance of re-joining Barcelona permanently as the Spain international targets a move to Paris Saint-Germain. Personal terms have been agreed between the European champions and Torres with an official bid expected soon.

‌



The 26-year-old is fresh of a historic achievement after scoring a World Cup-winning goal for Spain. He also helped Barca lift the La Liga title with 16 goals in 33 appearances. Despite his return, Torres did not make regular starting XI's which may be a factor in his decision to look for a move elsewhere

‌



When Raphinha was fit, Rashford also played a secondary role at Barcelona but he and Torres linked up on several occasions. Robert Lewandowksi was often preferred to the latter but he has since joined MLS side Chicago Fire.

‌



Michael Carrick provides Marcus Rashford update and confirms Man Utd star's next move READ MORE :

Despite that, the former Manchester City star is not guaranteed a place with the signings of Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon, which appeared to shut the door on Rashford's prospects of joining on a permanent basis, strengthening Barca's frontline.

While the new arrivals are not in direct competition with Torres, he may well be sensing that he is being sidelined. Head coach Hansi Flick also appeared open to the player departing when quizzed about his future following a 1-0 pre-season victory over Nottingham Forest.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



He said: "I respect all the players, I don't know anything about the situation at the moment. I was focused on the team, and I don't know anything."

Just hours before Barca's win over the Premier League side, Manchester United played out a 1-1 draw against Torres' potential future club PSG. Rashford played no part, still enjoying his post-World Cup break.

Michael Carrick did, however, confirm that he and two other players would be joining the club's pre-season camp in the coming days as preparations ramp up ahead of fixtures against Leeds United and AC Milan.

‌



The United head coach said: "We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together. "Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie [Mainoo] and Lisandro [Martinez]. We look forward to seeing them."

View 2 Images Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford will be back at Manchester United next week (Image: Getty Images)

Rashford currently looks more likely to stay put at Old Trafford, though a departure for Torres could certainly shake things up. Barca appear to have their sights set primarily on Manchester City's Rodri for now, but may well find themselves turning their attention to more attacking targets before long.

‌



Julian Alvarez is thought to be higher up their wishlist than Rashford, with Barca pursuing his signature intensely ahead of the World Cup.

The Argentine is said to still be seeking a move away, but Diego Simeone's side have no plans to negotiate with Barca unless his eye-watering release clause is triggered - which could enhance Rashford's prospects.
