World.title: NPFL: Shooting Stars part ways with Head Coach Aweroro after historic campaign
World.content:
Shooting Stars SC have parted ways with head coach Nurudeen Aweroro just days before the start of the new Nigeria Premier Football League season, bringing an abrupt end to his time in charge of the Oluyole Warriors.

The Ibadan club confirmed the development in an official statement, announcing that Aweroro, Team Manager Tammy Tamuno and Assistant Coach Shakiru Lawal have all left their respective positions with immediate effect.

Shooting Stars did not disclose the specific reasons behind the decision, describing the departure as a mutual agreement following discussions between the club and members of the technical team.

However, sources indicate that lingering issues between Aweroro and some influential members of the club’s board contributed to the sudden change.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In its statement, Shooting Stars said the affected members of the technical team had agreed to end their contracts amicably.

“We have reached a mutual agreement with Head Coach Nurudeen Aweroro, Team Manager Tammy Tamuno and Assistant Coach Shakiru Lawal to bring their respective contracts with the Club to an end, with immediate effect,” the club stated.

“The decision follows discussions between the Club and the affected members of the technical team, with both parties agreeing to part ways amicably.”

The club also praised the trio for their commitment and contributions, particularly their role in Shooting Stars’ impressive campaign last season.

“Shooting Stars appreciates Nurudeen Aweroro, Tammy Tamuno and Shakiru Lawal for their commitment, professionalism and contributions to the Club during their respective periods of service,” the statement added.

“The Club particularly acknowledges their efforts in helping Shooting Stars achieve a third-place finish in the 2025/26 NPFL season and secure a continental ticket.”

The club wished all three officials success in their future careers before announcing that its remaining assistant coaches would temporarily oversee the technical department.

“In the interim, the other Assistant Coaches have been directed to take charge of the affairs of the Technical Department pending the appointment and announcement of a substantive Head Coach. The Club will communicate further developments in due course.”

Aweroro leaves after historic NPFL campaign

The timing of Aweroro’s departure has added to the surprise surrounding the decision.

Shooting Stars parted ways with the coach on the eve of their participation in the Value Jet Cup pre-season tournament, just 24 hours after the Oluyole Warriors suffered a 3-0 friendly defeat to Ikorodu City.

Aweroro was appointed Shooting Stars head coach in July 2025 and went on to oversee one of the club’s most significant campaigns in recent years.

The Ibadan-based side finished third in the 2025/26 NPFL season, securing a place in the CAF Confederation Cup.

The achievement was particularly significant as it marked Shooting Stars’ first qualification for continental football in 27 years.

The club specifically acknowledged the contributions of Aweroro, Tamuno and Lawal to that historic accomplishment.

Now, however, the Oluyole Warriors must begin the new campaign without the coach who guided them back to continental competition.

World.title: EKO 2026: Sanwo-Olu inspects Lagos facilities ahead of National Intermediate Games
World.content:
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has inspected ongoing rehabilitation works at the Teslim Balogun Stadium and other sports facilities ahead of the inaugural National Intermediate Sports Festival, EKO 2026.

Mr Sanwo-Olu, in a post on his social media platforms on Saturday, said the state was making progress with preparations to host thousands of young athletes from across Nigeria.

According to the governor, the natural-grass pitch at Teslim Balogun Stadium has been completed, while work on the new tartan track is expected to be finished in the coming weeks.

He added that indoor halls, swimming pools and other sports facilities were also being upgraded ahead of the Games.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The natural grass pitch is complete, while work on the new tartan track will be finished in the coming weeks,” Mr Sanwo-Olu said.

“Our indoor halls, swimming pools and other facilities are also being upgraded to receive the thousands of young athletes expected from across the country.”

The governor said the rehabilitation of sports facilities was part of the state’s broader investment in grassroots sports development.

“For the past three years, we have been rebuilding sports centres across Surulere, Ikorodu, Epe, Agege and Badagry, because our young people deserve quality facilities close to home,” he said.

“We want them to discover their talents, compete with confidence and see a future for themselves in sports right here in Nigeria.”

EKO 2026 preparations

The inspection comes weeks after Lagos unveiled the official logo and mascot for EKO 2026, marking another milestone in preparations for the maiden edition of the National Intermediate Games.

The Games are scheduled to be held from 1 to 15 October 2026. They are expected to bring together young athletes from all 36 states, the Federal Capital Territory, and eligible Nigerian athletes from the diaspora.

The National Sports Commission conceived the Intermediate Games as a structured pathway between the National Youth Games and the National Sports Festival to identify and develop young talents before they progress to elite competition.

Speaking at the logo and mascot unveiling in July, the Director-General of the Lagos State Sports Commission, Lekan Fatodu, said the state was committed to delivering a successful first edition.

Mr Fatodu said rehabilitation work at the Teslim Balogun Stadium was progressing according to schedule and that the state was also working with private institutions to provide additional venues.

He specifically mentioned the British International School in Lekki as one of the private facilities secured through partnerships for the Games.

The Director-General of the National Sports Commission, Bukola Olopade, had also explained that Lagos was chosen as the host because of its established grassroots sports development structure.

He said the state had demonstrated a system capable of identifying athletes from the school level and developing them towards elite competition.

Mr Olopade said the Games would help bridge the gap between youth-level competitions and the National Sports Festival, providing young athletes with a more structured route into higher-level sports.

The commission also planned diaspora trials in London for eligible Nigerian athletes abroad, with successful participants expected to compete in Lagos.

With less than two months to the opening of the Games, Mr Sanwo-Olu said Lagos was ready to welcome the next generation of Nigerian athletes.

“Lagos is ready, and we look forward to welcoming the next generation of Nigerian athletes,” the governor said.
