World.title: How technology enabled customs transformation — Adeniyi
World.content:
Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Adewale Adeniyi

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

ABUJA — The Comptroller-General of Customs, Mr Adewale Adeniyi, has attributed the transformation of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) to the deliberate deployment of technology across virtually every aspect of Customs administration.

Adeniyi spoke during a two-day retreat between the NCS and the Senate Committee on Customs and Excise in Abuja, aimed at strengthening legislative oversight and reviewing the Nigeria Customs Service Act.

In a statement issued by the Customs spokesman, Abdullahi Maiwada, Deputy Comptroller, on Sunday, the Comptroller-General said technology had enabled the Service to improve the speed and efficiency of its operations.

He said, “Technology helps us to work faster and more efficiently. We started by deploying digital solutions into personnel administration, postings, staff matters and pensions before extending them to our core operational responsibilities, and we will continue until virtually every aspect of Customs operations is technology-driven.”

Adeniyi said the Service had also introduced advanced technological solutions into its enforcement operations, including virtual shooting simulators, geospatial intelligence and digital surveillance.

“We are deploying geospatial intelligence to map our patrol routes and position our checkpoints more efficiently across the country. Combined with modern training facilities such as our virtual shooting range, these innovations will significantly strengthen our enforcement capabilities,” he said.

The Customs boss added that the Nigeria Customs Service Act provided the legal backing for several of the Service’s modernisation initiatives.

He said, “The law requires us to modernise our operations. Initiatives such as the Authorised Economic Operator Programme, Advance Ruling, Time Release Study, scanner deployment and other technology-driven reforms are all backed by the provisions of the Nigeria Customs Service Act.

“Our responsibility is to continue implementing them to support the Federal Government reform agenda.”

In his remarks, the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Customs and Excise, Senator Isah Jibrin, expressed satisfaction with the reforms introduced under Adeniyi’s leadership.

Jibrin said the reforms demonstrated efforts to improve the efficiency of the NCS and the utilisation of resources allocated to the Service.

He said the visit enabled lawmakers to witness the transformation of the Service firsthand.

“We have heard about these reforms from afar, but today we have seen them ourselves. The transformation taking place in the NCS is remarkable, particularly in the deployment of technology, modern infrastructure and operational innovations that are repositioning the Service for greater efficiency,” he said.

The senator added that the retreat had given lawmakers a clearer understanding of how funds appropriated to the Service were being deployed.

“When the NCS comes before the National Assembly seeking approval for capital expenditure, we now have a clearer understanding of what those resources are being used for.

“The reforms we have seen today clearly demonstrate that government funds are being invested responsibly to strengthen Customs operations, improve trade facilitation and enhance national revenue,” he said.

As part of the programme, members of the committee toured the Customs House in Maitama, Abuja, where they were briefed on the Service’s ongoing modernisation initiatives, technology-driven operations and institutional reforms.

World.title: Padded budget, wasteful expenditures fuelling insecurity – Atiku
World.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar

…Says, with 5,091 killed in 3 months, Tinubu”s scorecard soaked in blood

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has blamed padded budgets and wasteful government expenditure for Nigeria’s worsening insecurity, describing reports that 5,091 Nigerians were killed in violent incidents across the country within three months as a damning scorecard on the President Bola Tinubu administration’s most fundamental responsibility of protecting lives and property.

“Today, we have 5,091 reported killings in just three months, 5,091 shattered families, 5,091 indictments of this administration’s security failures, and ultimately, 5,091 reasons this government must go”, he declared.

In a statement on Sunday in Abuja, his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu, said the figures were not merely statistics but a grim measure of the human cost of insecurity and the consequences of a government that has failed to match its rhetoric with the resources, discipline and urgency required to protect Nigerians.

“Behind every number is a Nigerian whose life was cut short, a family thrown into mourning, children deprived of parents and communities condemned to fear. Five thousand and ninety-one reported killings in just three months should trouble the conscience of any government.

“These figures are the human cost of every padded budget, every frivolous expenditure and every failure to fully implement funds appropriated for critical national priorities. You cannot run the public treasury as though it were a private purse, squander scarce resources on questionable priorities and then expect soldiers and other security personnel on the frontlines to perform miracles,” he said.

The Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, said the practice of treating fiscal appropriation as an inconvenience while public resources are diverted to politically expedient projects continues to undermine national security and weaken the capacity of the Armed Forces and other agencies to respond decisively to threats.

While welcoming the recently announced pay increase for military personnel, Atiku said improved remuneration, though necessary, represents only a fraction of what is required to restore morale and strengthen operational effectiveness among troops on the frontlines.

“Our soldiers deserve better pay, but morale is about much more than salaries. They require adequate equipment, operational funding, timely allowances, proper welfare for their families and the assurance that the government they defend is as committed to their mission as they are,” he said.

He insisted that Nigerians deserve a government that cuts waste, eliminates questionable expenditure and substantially improves the implementation of budgetary appropriations, particularly for defence and security.

“A government that cannot protect its citizens has failed the first test of governance. Nigerians cannot continue to pay with their lives for the failures, waste and misplaced priorities of an administration that has failed in its most basic constitutional duty,” he said.

Atiku added that every Nigerian lost to terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other violent crimes represents a failure of the state, noting that the victims were fathers, mothers, sons, daughters and breadwinners who had every right to expect protection from their government.

World.title: 19-year-old struck dead by thunder in Enugu community
World.content:
By Alumona Ukwueze

NSUKKA —-A 19-year-old man, Chukwujekwu Eyah, has reportedly been struck dead by thunder while sleeping with four other boys at his maternal grandmother’s residence.

The death occurred in Ogboli, Ugbaike, Enugu Ezike, Igbo-Eze North Local Government Area of Enugu State.

The incident reportedly occurred at about 1 a.m. on Monday, with Eyah dying in the incident while the four other boys sleeping on the same bed were left unharmed.

The police have yet to officially comment on the matter, but relations of the deceased confirmed his death, saying he was buried on Wednesday.

One of the relations said, “Chukwujekwu was buried on Wednesday. He died around 1 a.m. at Ogboli in Ugbaike, Enugu Ezike, Igbo-Eze North Local Government Area.

“Master Chukwujekwu was asleep when the incident occurred at his maternal grandparents’ residence. We have done our investigations.”

The relations, however, attributed the incident to a traditional belief concerning instruments reportedly used by Eyah’s late father, who they said was known as a rain-maker.

According to them, Eyah had gone to the instruments kept at his mother’s residence in Iheaka, in neighbouring Igbo-Eze South Local Government Area, without performing what they described as the required traditional rituals.

They claimed that the thunder subsequently struck Eyah alone while he was sleeping with the other four boys, without causing injuries to them or damaging any property or animal in the house.

The relations said they received news of his death around 8 a.m. and conducted what they described as a traditional investigation through divination.

They further alleged that Eyah’s late father had taken the instruments, which they said were used to cause or prevent rainfall, from his wife’s family in Iheaka but that the family failed to return them after his death.

They said the traditional belief in the community was that such instruments should either be properly maintained according to tradition or returned to their original owners.

The circumstances surrounding the teenager’s death could not be independently verified, while the police had yet to issue an official statement on the incident.

World.title: Full list of countries being led by female presidents in 2026
World.content:
Women continue to make their mark at the highest levels of political leadership, with female presidents currently serving as heads of state in countries across Africa, Europe, Asia, the Americas and the Pacific.

Although women remain underrepresented in national leadership globally, a growing number have reached the presidency through elections, appointments or succession.

Their presence has added to the changing political landscape in countries ranging from Mexico and India to Namibia, Tanzania and Iceland.

As of 2026, the following 16 countries have women serving as presidents.

1. Bulgaria – Iliana Iotova

Iliana Iotova became Bulgaria’s president in January 2026, taking over the country’s highest office after previously serving as vice president.

Her elevation added Bulgaria to the growing list of countries with women occupying the presidency.

2. Costa Rica – Laura Fernández Delgado

Laura Fernández Delgado became president of Costa Rica in May 2026.

Her election placed another woman at the head of a Latin American country and continued Costa Rica’s history of female representation at the highest level of government.

3. Dominica – Sylvanie Burton

Sylvanie Burton has served as president of Dominica since October 2023.

She made history by becoming the first woman and first Indigenous president of Dominica. The presidency is largely ceremonial, with executive authority resting primarily with the prime minister.

4. Iceland – Halla Tómasdóttir

Halla Tómasdóttir became Iceland’s president in August 2024 after winning the country’s presidential election.

She succeeded Guðni Jóhannesson and became Iceland’s second woman president, following Vigdís Finnbogadóttir, who served from 1980 to 1996.

5. India – Droupadi Murmu

Droupadi Murmu became India’s president in July 2022 after winning the presidential election.

She is the first person from India’s tribal communities to serve as president and only the second woman to hold the office.

As president, Murmu serves as India’s constitutional head of state, while executive authority is exercised by the elected government led by the prime minister.

6. Ireland – Catherine Connolly

Catherine Connolly became president of Ireland in November 2025.

Her victory marked another milestone in Ireland’s political history and made her the country’s 11th president.

The Irish presidency is primarily a ceremonial and constitutional office, with the government headed by the taoiseach.

7. Malta – Myriam Spiteri Debono

Myriam Spiteri Debono has served as president of Malta since April 2024.

She became the island nation’s 11th president and one of several women to have held Malta’s highest constitutional office.

8. Marshall Islands – Hilda Heine

Hilda Heine returned to the presidency of the Marshall Islands in January 2024.

She previously served as president between 2016 and 2020, becoming the first woman to lead the Pacific island nation.

Her return to office made her one of the relatively small number of women serving as national presidents worldwide.

9. Mexico – Claudia Sheinbaum

Claudia Sheinbaum became president of Mexico in October 2024, making history as the first woman to serve as president of Mexico.

Before entering national office, Sheinbaum served as mayor of Mexico City and built a political career within the Morena party.

Her election represented a major milestone for Mexico, one of Latin America’s largest and most influential countries.

10. Moldova – Maia Sandu

Maia Sandu has served as president of Moldova since December 2020.

She became the country’s first woman president after defeating incumbent Igor Dodon in the 2020 election.

Sandu was subsequently re-elected, securing another term in office and remaining one of Europe’s most prominent female heads of state.

11. Namibia – Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah

Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah became Namibia’s president in March 2025.

She made history as Namibia’s first female president, becoming one of Africa’s women to reach the highest political office in their country.

Before becoming president, she served as Namibia’s vice president and held several senior government positions.

12. North Macedonia – Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova

Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova became president of North Macedonia in May 2024.

She made history as the first woman elected president of the country.

A university professor and constitutional law expert, Siljanovska-Davkova entered the presidential race as the candidate of the opposition VMRO-DPMNE party.

13. Slovenia – Nataša Pirc Musar

Nataša Pirc Musar became president of Slovenia in December 2022.

She defeated centre-right politician Anže Logar in the presidential election to become Slovenia’s first female president.

Before entering politics, Pirc Musar was known for her work as a lawyer, journalist and Slovenia’s information commissioner.

14. Suriname – Jennifer Geerlings-Simons

Jennifer Geerlings-Simons became president of Suriname in July 2025.

Her election marked a historic moment for the South American country, as she became its first woman president.

Geerlings-Simons previously served as president of Suriname’s National Assembly and had a long career in national politics.

15. Tanzania – Samia Suluhu Hassan

Samia Suluhu Hassan has served as Tanzania’s president since March 2021.

She became president following the death of President John Magufuli, having previously served as his vice president.

She subsequently won election in her own right and became Tanzania’s first woman president.

Her presidency also made her one of the most prominent female political leaders in Africa.

16. Trinidad and Tobago – Christine Kangaloo

Christine Kangaloo became president of Trinidad and Tobago in March 2023.

She is the second woman to serve as president of the Caribbean country, following Kamla Persad-Bissessar’s earlier tenure as prime minister rather than president.

Kangaloo previously served as president of the Senate and held several ministerial positions before becoming head of state.

World.title: Fire service rescues 16 from collapsed building in Kano
World.content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

The Kano State Fire Service has rescued 16 people after a residential building collapsed in the Dan Dishe area of Kwanar Yashi, Fagge Local Government Area of the state.

The incident happened in the early hours of Saturday, when the building, said to be about 20 by 30 feet, suddenly collapsed.

The spokesperson of the Kano State Fire Service, Saminu Abdullahi, confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the agency received an emergency call at about 4:32 a.m.

According to him, the distress call was made by one of the service’s staff members, Aminu Sani Warure, who alerted the emergency response unit about the collapse.

Abdullahi said firefighters were quickly dispatched from the service headquarters to the affected area.

“Upon receiving the report, men of the Service from the Headquarters were immediately mobilised to the scene,” he said.

He explained that the rescue team searched through the debris and successfully brought out 16 people trapped inside the collapsed structure.

“Among those rescued were three children who were found unconscious,” the statement added.

They were identified as five-year-old Affan Yusuf, seven-year-old Hassana Yusuf and nine-month-old Ummulkursum Yusuf.

The fire service spokesperson said the exact reason the building collapsed had not been established.

He added that investigations were underway to determine what led to the incident.

The fire service also urged residents to take building and other safety measures seriously, especially during the rainy season when some structures may become more vulnerable.

The agency advised members of the public to observe necessary safety precautions to reduce the risk of similar incidents.

World.title: It’s a charade – Aggrieved NDC members reject Utomi, Galadima reconciliation committee
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — Aggrieved members of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) in Edo South Senatorial District have rejected the party’s national reconciliation committee, describing it as a charade that cannot heal the wounds of injustice caused by its leaders.

They said a stolen mandate cannot be reconciled away and stressed that injustice does not become legitimate simply because a committee has been established to manage the anger it created.

A statement issued by Agbonaye Osazee Ofo on behalf of the aggrieved members said the disputed election cannot be wished away. The members contended that the committee’s main objective is to persuade aggrieved members to accept an unfair outcome.

The statement read: “The decision by the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) to constitute a National Reconciliation Committee following its controversial primary elections is, on the surface, presented as an attempt to restore peace, unity, and cohesion within the party. But beneath the carefully chosen language of ‘reconciliation,’ ‘fairness,’ and ‘internal democracy’ lies a much more troubling question:”

Asking who is to be reconciled and on what terms, the statement noted: “A reconciliation committee cannot become a substitute for justice. It cannot be used to paper over disputed primaries, silence legitimate grievances, or compel aggrieved members to accept outcomes they firmly believe were imposed upon them.

“If the underlying disputes arose because members believe their mandates were manipulated, overturned, or denied, then the first responsibility of the NDC leadership should be to establish the truth — not to assemble a committee and expect the victims of the process to simply move on.”

The aggrieved members claimed the committee is not intended to reconcile anyone but to force compliance, saying: “This panel was never assembled to heal wounds; it was deployed to enforce compliance.

“It invites the betrayed to sit at a table set by those accused of betraying them, offering hollow assurances of peace in exchange for surrender.

“That is not reconciliation. That is an attempt to manufacture acceptance.

“You cannot rig the process, produce a disputed outcome, and then establish a committee to persuade those who lost their mandates to accept the result in the name of party unity.”

Ofo, speaking for other members, said: “Unity without justice is not unity. It is forced conformity.”

He urged the NDC leadership to understand that political parties do not become stronger by suppressing legitimate grievances. “They become stronger by confronting wrongdoing honestly and correcting it where necessary,” he said.

Maintaining that peace cannot be built on unresolved injustice, the group said the leadership’s declaration of commitment to “internal democracy, fairness, inclusiveness and party cohesion” raises an obvious question: Where were these principles when the disputed primaries were conducted?

The statement continued: “If fairness truly matters, let the party demonstrate it by reopening the issues that have generated controversy. If democracy matters, let genuine winners retain their mandates. If inclusiveness matters, let aggrieved aspirants and party members be heard without intimidation, manipulation, or predetermined conclusions.

“There can be no meaningful reconciliation where the facts remain contested, and the disputed outcomes are treated as untouchable. True peace cannot take root in the poisoned soil of unpunished injustice.”

A committee cannot legitimize a flawed process

“The appointment of respected personalities to the committee does not, by itself, confer legitimacy on the process that produced the disputes.

“Prof. Pat Utomi, Engr. Buba Galadima and the other members may bring credibility and experience to the assignment, but even the most respected individuals cannot transform an unjust process into a just one simply by sitting on a reconciliation panel.

“The real test is whether the committee has the independence and authority to question the party leadership, examine the primary-election records, hear all sides, overturn illegitimate decisions where necessary, and recommend the restoration of mandates where wrongdoing is established.”

The statement warned that anything less would amount to political theatre and emphasized that the aggrieved are not the problem.

“The NDC should stop treating those who are challenging disputed outcomes as obstacles to party unity. The real threat to party unity is not the member demanding justice.

“The real threat is a system that tells a legitimately aggrieved member: ‘Accept what happened or be accused of destroying the party.’ That is an unacceptable distortion of democratic principles.

“Members have every right to demand transparency. They have every right to question primary-election outcomes. They have every right to insist that their votes and mandates not be casually substituted by political calculations.

“And they should not be expected to surrender those rights merely because the 2027 elections are approaching.”

Reconciliation must begin with truth

“If the NDC genuinely wants reconciliation, then the committee should begin with the facts. Let the disputed primaries be examined. Let the competing claims be heard. Let the evidence be reviewed. Let the rules of the party be applied equally.

“Let anyone who benefited from an illegitimate process be prepared to have that outcome reviewed. And, most importantly, let the committee be free to make recommendations that may be uncomfortable for the party leadership. That is what genuine reconciliation looks like.

Anything short of that is merely an exercise in public relations.”

The aggrieved members said the NDC cannot campaign for democracy while practising the opposite.

“The NDC cannot credibly present itself to Nigerians as a democratic alternative while failing to resolve allegations of internal democratic violations within its own ranks.

“A party that seeks the mandate of Nigerians in 2027 must first demonstrate that it respects the mandates of its own members.

“You cannot preach democracy to the electorate while asking your own members to accept disputed outcomes without a credible remedy.

“You cannot demand public trust while refusing to confront internal mistrust. And you cannot build a credible national alternative on unresolved internal contradictions.”

They said that the talked-about unity would be achieved if the stolen mandates are returned.

According to the statement: “The message to the NDC leadership should therefore be unequivocal: Do not use reconciliation as a mechanism for legitimizing disputed outcomes.

“If the party truly believes in fairness, let it have the courage to dismantle illegitimate outcomes, restore mandates where the evidence demands it, and subject contested matters to genuinely independent arbitration.

“Until that happens, this reconciliation committee risks becoming nothing more than a hollow charade — a desperate attempt to cover a festering wound without treating its cause.”

The statement added that the NDC does not need forced peace.

“It needs justice before reconciliation, truth before unity, and democracy before electoral expediency. Anything else is merely an insult to the very democratic values the party claims to uphold.

“A stolen mandate cannot be reconciled away. A disputed election cannot be wished away. And injustice cannot become legitimate simply because a committee has been established to manage the anger it created.”

The aggrieved members said they view the committee as intended to endorse or validate injustice rather than correct it.

They said the reconciliation effort is seen as legitimizing manipulated mandates and as an attempt to persuade aggrieved members to accept an unfair outcome.

“Let it be on record that this is completely unacceptable. It is a blatant affront to fairness, justice, and due process, and it must not be tolerated,” they added.

World.title: Osun election: ADC’s Salaam not in alliance with any party, will contest to win — Aregbesola
World.content:
Former Governor of Osun State and National Secretary of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola, has dismissed reports that the party and its governorship candidate, Rt. Hon. Dr. Najeem Folasayo Salaam, have withdrawn from the forthcoming Osun State governorship election or entered into an alliance with another political party.

Aregbesola described the reports as false, unfounded and misleading, urging members of the public to disregard them.

He spoke on Saturday at a solidarity rally held in Ejigbo, Osun State, to celebrate the 61st birthday of Salaam and reaffirm support for his candidacy.

The former governor said the ADC remained firmly committed to the governorship contest, stressing that the party had neither withdrawn from the election nor entered into any alliance with another political party.

According to him, the party has built a formidable political structure founded on progressive ideals, principles and traditions, making it unnecessary for the ADC to abandon its electoral ambition.

“The ADC is too strong and too well-positioned to negotiate away its political ambition or contemplate an alliance with any other political party. We have built a formidable structure anchored on progressive principles, ideals and traditions.

“We have absolute faith in God and confidence in the support of the people. We are contesting this election to win.”

Aregbesola also praised Salaam’s personal qualities, describing him as a man of integrity, humility, exemplary character and compassion for humanity.

He said these qualities had distinguished the ADC candidate as a leader worthy of public trust, urging the people of Osun State to support the party and its governorship candidate.

The former governor expressed confidence that a Salaam-led administration would restore the dignity of progressive ideals and renew the people’s confidence in democracy, good governance and purposeful leadership.

Speaking at the event, Salaam thanked supporters, political associates and well-wishers for their longstanding support, goodwill and affection throughout his political journey.

He described the birthday celebration and solidarity rally as a gesture he deeply cherished, assuring his supporters that their confidence in him would be reciprocated through dedicated and quality service to humanity.

Salaam further reaffirmed his commitment to his manifesto, describing it as a solemn promise to the people of Osun State.

He appealed to the electorate to support the ADC in the forthcoming governorship election, promising that his administration, if elected, would pursue purposeful, inclusive and people-centred governance.

The event, held in Ejigbo, attracted a large gathering of ADC supporters, political associates, community leaders and well-wishers who came together to celebrate Salaam’s 61st birthday and reaffirm their support for his governorship ambition.

World.title: ‎Police, army comb forests for Kogi kidnapped victims, destroy suspected hideouts
World.content:
By Boluwaji Obahopo

‎

‎Security forces in Kogi State have intensified search and rescue operations following a kidnapping incident along the Okene-Auchi Road, combing suspected criminal hideouts in forests around the Okene-Ajaokuta axis.

‎

‎The operation, involving the police, Nigerian Army and Edo State Police Command, has also seen the deployment of drones to enhance surveillance and intelligence gathering as security agencies intensify efforts to rescue the victims and apprehend their abductors.

‎

‎The Kogi State Police Command, in a statement on Sunday by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Saliu Oyiza Afusat, said the operation was launched immediately after the incident, with intelligence-driven bush-combing operations conducted across identified forest corridors, particularly the Ebiya Forest and adjoining areas.

‎

‎”The operation involves personnel from the Area Command, Okene; 77 Police Mobile Force Squadron, Okene; Okene and Adavi Divisions; Anti-Kidnapping Unit; Violent Crime Response Unit and detachments of the Nigerian Army operating from Forward Operating Bases in the area.

‎

‎”The Edo State Police Command has also deployed its Anti-Kidnapping Unit and other tactical personnel to support the operation, particularly along the Kogi-Edo border.

‎

‎”Security teams have identified and searched suspected criminal hideouts in the forest, recovering foodstuffs and cooking ingredients, an Army-pattern jungle hat, a National Identity Card and other items suspected to have been abandoned by the criminals.

‎

‎”The suspected hideouts were subsequently destroyed and set ablaze to prevent the criminals from returning to use them.”

‎

‎The statement, however, said no kidnapped victim was recovered during the initial phase of the operation, stressing that security forces had continued advancing into the forest and adjoining areas in search of the victims.

‎

‎“Technical support, including the deployment of drones by the Nigerian Army and Edo State Police Command, is also being utilised to enhance surveillance and intelligence gathering during the operation,” the statement said.

‎

‎The Commissioner of Police, Kogi State Command, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, psc, mni, directed the operational teams to sustain the search and rescue operation until the victims were safely recovered and the perpetrators apprehended.

‎

‎He assured residents that the command was working closely with sister security agencies and relevant stakeholders to ensure that the perpetrators did not escape justice.

‎

‎The command appealed to residents, particularly those living around the affected areas, to remain calm and vigilant and provide security agencies with timely and credible information that could assist the ongoing operation.

‎

‎..Police restore calm in Abugi

‎

‎Meanwhile, the police command said it had restored calm to Abugi and adjoining communities following recent reprisal killings in the area.

‎

‎The command said the Area Command, Lokoja, in collaboration with security and community stakeholders, had engaged traditional rulers, community leaders and other stakeholders in efforts to prevent further escalation and restore peaceful coexistence.

‎

‎It said the engagements focused on reconciliation and addressing the underlying causes of the conflict, while security personnel remained strategically deployed in the affected communities to protect lives and property.

‎

‎The command also said the State Criminal Investigation Department had commenced a full-scale investigation into the killings, with efforts underway to identify, trace and arrest persons found to have participated in or contributed to the violence.

‎

‎It warned that the restoration of peace would not affect the investigation, stressing that anyone found culpable would be prosecuted in accordance with the law.

‎

‎The Commissioner of Police urged residents across the state to remain law-abiding and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to the police and other security agencies.

‎

‎He reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property and maintaining peace across the state.

‎

World.title: ARISE News Hosts Osun 2026 Governorship Town Hall
World.content:
ARISE News is set to host a special televised town hall bringing together leading candidates in the 2026 Osun State governorship election ahead of the poll.

The town hall is scheduled for Tuesday, August 11, 2026, at the Aurora Conference & Event Centre, Ring Road, Osogbo, with the livestream commencing at 11am.

The confirmed participants include Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party; Munirudeen Bola Oyebanji of the All Progressives Congress (APC); and Dr. Najeem Salaam of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

Themed 2026 Governorship Election: The Battle for Osun State, the special forum is expected to focus attention on the key issues shaping the 2026 governorship contest and provide voters with an opportunity to hear directly from the leading contenders ahead of the Saturday August 15 governorship election.

The town hall will be broadcast and livestreamed by ARISE News from 11am on Tuesday.

World.title: Women Group Decries Senate’s Confirmation of Fasina As Ambassador
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

Over 300 women’s rights organizations have rejected the Nigerian Senate’s confirmation of Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina as Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, citing alleged disregard for pending sexual harassment cases and due process.

In a petition signed by Co-Convener of Womanifesto, Wumi Asubiaro-Dada, the groups described the Senate’s action as “a charade of shame, travesty of justice and in total oblivion of existing petitions”.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio confirmed Fasina during plenary, citing four reasons: that the nominee is from Lagos State with no opposition, that no petition was submitted against him, the principle of presumption of innocence, and that the police and FUOYE Governing Council had cleared him.

The coalition disputed all four points while insisting that Fasina is from Abeokuta South Local Government Area of Ogun State, despite being educated in Lagos, and not an indigene of Lagos State.

The groups said two petitions dated June 25, 2026 and June 29, 2026, with acknowledged copies, were submitted to the Office of the Senate President and the Chairman, Senate Committee on Foreign Affairs, adding that also attached were details of two suits pending at the National Industrial Court.

According to the petition, “Ambassadorial appointments demand public confidence, ethical credibility and demonstrable respect for accountability processes. Confirming a nominee while multiple judicial proceedings remain pending sends a dangerous signal to survivors of workplace sexual harassment.

“The first, Suit No. NICN/ABJ/201/2025, is a sexual harassment case filed by a FUOYE staffer. The petitioners said it is supported by a 37-minute audio recording allegedly of Prof. Fasina. The second, Suit No. NICN/LA/61/2025, alleges harassment and victimization.

“The complainant claims she was denied promotion and later had her appointment terminated after rejecting alleged advances, in violation of a court order to maintain peace.”

The groups also challenged claims that Fasina had been cleared, arguing that the police lack constitutional powers to give final clearance on sexual harassment allegations and that the FUOYE panel that dismissed the case was composed of university employees under the control of the then vice-chancellor.

On the issue of appearance before the Senate, the CSOs said no invitation was extended to the complainants or civil society groups, contrary to the Senate’s claim that victims “failed to appear”. They cited Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution on the right to fair hearing.

The petition further referenced House of Representatives records indicating that Folasade Adebayo submitted over 100 pages of evidence and travelled to Abuja on May 14, 2025 for a scheduled hearing.

The hearing was postponed indefinitely after Fasina allegedly failed to respond to the committee’s invitation.

The CSOs also stated that the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) commenced an investigation in 2025 into allegations of abuse of office and sexual harassment.

They alleged that Fasina obtained a court order restraining the ICPC and that the matter remained pending.

World.title: Umo Eno At Yoruba Tennis Club
World.content:
Etim Etim

Yoruba Tennis Club (YTC), Onikan, Lagos was founded in 1926 by a group of 25 young Nigerians to provide sporting, recreational and social facilities for Nigerians who were not admitted into similar facilities owned and managed by the colonial authorities then. Lagos was then a highly segregated town, with the British colonial officers working on the Marina and living in Ikoyi. Nigerians were not allowed to go near Ikoyi. The closest they came close was Onikan, some three or four kilometres away.

This year marks the centenary anniversary of YTC which, expectedly, has grown in membership from the initial 25 to over 2,000 today. It is one of the most prestigious social clubs in Lagos, in the same league with Ikoyi Club, founded in 1928 and Ikeja Country Club. A series of yearlong activities have been designed to commemorate the milestone anniversary, including anniversary lectures to be given by a reputable thought leader. The first was delivered by Prof. Wole Soyinka in February, the second by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State in April and the third by Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom on Thursday, August 8.

A member of the club, Air Commodore Demola Onitiju (rtd), said Governor Eno was chosen ‘’because of his exceptional performance in office in the last three years; his grasp of the concept of good governance and public administration, and understanding of the ideals of what the Yoruba refers to as ‘omoluabi’ which emphasizes openness, good governance and transparency’’. Eno’s presentation was titled ‘Democracy and Good Governance: Renewing Hope in Challenging Times.’

The hall was packed full. The presence of Eno’s predecessor, Udom Emmanuel; Governor Babajide Sawon-olu; business leaders and politicians, as well as leaders and members of the club added considerable prestige to the event. From Akwa Ibom State came a large delegation of government officials; politicians and elders, among whom were Atuekong Don Etiebet; Paul Usoro (SAN); Emmanuel Enoidem (SAN); Senators Effiong Bob; Aloysius Etok and Ekong Sampson. There was a colourful contingent of members of Akwa Ibom community in Lagos, as well as Lagos business class, prominent among whom was Mr. Tony Ndah, a renowned quantity surveyor and project management consultant.

Eno opened his lecture with a philosophical look at the circumstances that gave birth to the Yoruba Tennis Club. He said: ‘’The Europeans in this city had their own club, and no African, however educated, however accomplished, was thought fit to walk through its doors. Our fathers did not stand at that gate and beg. They went and built their own house. They approached the colonial government for a piece of land at Onikan. They raised money for the first court from their own pockets, in cash and in kind, and they opened it before that year was out. At a general meeting in September of that same year, several names were put forward, but the members chose the Yoruba Tennis Club, a name it still answers to today.

‘’A group of citizens looked at an injustice, organised themselves, raised their own resources, built an institution, wrote rules for it, and handed it down so faithfully that one hundred years later we are seated inside it. And having called it ‘Yoruba’, they deliberately kept its doors open to Nigerians of every origin who could keep its creed of honesty, integrity and industry’’. Eno then paid tributes to the founding fathers of the club as true visionaries. ‘’Vision is common. Vision that outlives the visionary is rare, and that’s what this club embodies,” he enthused.

Delving into his lecture, the governor argued that democracies around the world are going through severe stress tests as never before in a generation by economic pressures, insecurity, climate shocks, youth unemployment, technological disruption and a steady erosion of public trust have made citizens everywhere anxious and impatient. Nigeria is also experiencing these problems, but it is in a moment like this that nations are being rebuilt, he noted. To that extent, leaders have a responsibility to not only preserve democracy, but to also make it meaningful. ‘’A citizen does not experience democracy on Election Day alone. He experiences it at the hospital gate, in his child’s classroom, on the road to his farm, and in the price of what he eats. A democracy that never reaches those places loses its moral authority long before it loses an election,’’ the governor deadpanned. He received a sustained applause.

In other words, democracy must be measured by the quality of governance it produces, guided by participation, transparency, accountability, equity and rule of law. Nigerians, the governor continued, should choose their leaders wisely and peacefully and hold their leaders accountable. He then concluded by illustrating how his administration apply these principles through the ARISE Agenda with investments in education, health, youth empowerment, infrastructure and compassionate homes.

The lecture ended with a Q&A session with club members asking questions on incentives for investments in the state; the new Ibom International Hospital being constructed and how the governor ensures there’s integrity in what he does.

The Yoruba Tennis Club provided a national platform for the Eno administration to tell his story, and he did so brilliantly in 50 minutes, even with all the applauses.

* Etim, a journalist, writes from Abuja

World.title: Colombia Announces Change of Position, Recognizes Morocco’s Sovereignty Over Sahara
World.content:
Colombia has announced the change of its position on the Sahara issue and affirmed its recognition of the Kingdom of Morocco’s sovereignty over its Southern Provinces.

According to a statement by Morocco’s foreign ministry, this new position was announced on Friday during the meeting held between the Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation, and Moroccan Expatriates, and the Vice-President of the Republic of Colombia, Mr. José Manuel Restrepo, attended by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Mr Omar Bula Escobar.

“On this occasion, Mr Bula Escobar affirmed that Colombia “recognizes Morocco’s sovereignty over its Sahara,” enshrining a new orientation for Colombia’s position on this issue.

“For his part, Mr Restrepo underlined that this announcement marks ‘a new beginning’ for ties between Colombia and Morocco, adding that the Kingdom is “Colombia’s first ally in Africa,”the statement said.

It added that, “In this respect, he expressed his country’s determination to establish a strategic partnership with Morocco.”

Meanwhile, Mr Bourita described Colombia’s decision to withdraw its recognition of the pseudo ‘sadr’ and recognize Morocco’s sovereignty over its Sahara as “historic,” stressing that it could give “great momentum” to bilateral ties.

He pointed out that Morocco and Colombia could represent economic platforms for each other by taking advantage of their respective positions in Africa and in Latin America.

Mr Bourita affirmed that his presence in Cali, on the Very High Instructions of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, to represent the Sovereign in the investiture ceremony of new President Abelardo de la Espriella, embodies the Kingdom’s determination to support this new momentum and elevate relations between Morocco and Colombia to a higher level.

This decision has added Colombia to a growing number of countries that are withdrawing recognition of the pseudo ‘sard’, and instead support the UN-led political process.

Earlier in the year, Bolivia, Mali and Honduras also announced the suspension of their recognition of the so- called ‘sard’. In addition, a number of countries have recognised Morocco’s sovereignty over its southern provinces in the Sahara and supported the country’s Autonomy Plan as a credible and realistic solution to the dispute.

World.title: Leo Stan Ekeh Champions Character Reforms, Empowers Community Leaders
World.content:
For Dr. Leo Stan Ekeh, Chairman of Zinox Group, true philanthropy is measured not by the size of donations but by the lives transformed. Over the years, the tech icon has built a reputation as one of Nigeria’s most impactful corporate citizens, channeling his influence and resources into initiatives that nurture ethical leadership, education and community development.

It was therefore unsurprising when The Leo Stan Ekeh Foundation partnered the Nkata Ndi Iyom Igbo Foundation to stage a four-day regional Train-the-Trainers seminar aimed at promoting character development and values-based leadership across South-east Nigeria.

Held under the theme, “Rebuilding Character, Strengthening Values, Empowering Minds, Enabling the Future,” the programme attracted women, teachers, mothers and community leaders from the five South-east states, alongside participants from Edo and Delta States. The initiative sought to equip attendees with practical skills to become advocates of moral reorientation and positive social change within their communities.

The seminar featured intensive sessions on behavioural change, emotional intelligence, etiquette, mentoring, leadership and effective communication, all facilitated by respected experts in education and human development.

Declaring the programme open, the Vice-Chancellor of Imo State University, Prof. U.U. Chukwumaeze, urged participants to embrace the collective responsibility of raising a generation rooted in integrity, discipline, respect and communal values, stressing that national development begins with sound character.

Director of The Leo Stan Ekeh Foundation, Prof. Gloria Ernest-Samuel, expressed confidence that participants would return home as certified trainers capable of inspiring positive change in families, schools, faith-based organisations and youth groups.

The initiative further strengthened the partnership between The Leo Stan Ekeh Foundation, the Nkata Ndi Iyom Igbo Foundation, founded by former Minister of Women Affairs, Iyom Josephine Anenih, and Imo State University. Beyond the seminar, the collaboration reflects Ekeh’s enduring belief that rebuilding society begins with rebuilding character, one community at a time.

World.title: DECISION TIME IN OSUN STATE…
World.content:
The choice of the people should prevail

Essentially because of the desperation by politicians, off-season elections that should ordinarily be easy to conduct are now riddled with controversies. Interestingly, this kind of election is an entirely Nigerian phenomenon. They started in 2006 primarily due to court rulings which overturned many election results before the 1999 Constitution was amended to legitimise the idea. But instead of enhancing public trust and building confidence in the electoral system, many of these stand-alone elections are now deepening the crisis of legitimacy. It is therefore little surprise that the campaigns for who becomes the next Governor of Osun State is turning out a puzzling spectacle.

Last Thursday, President Bola Tinubu, overruled the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) by directing a reversal of the freezing of the Osun State Government Statutory Allocation account. The action by the anti-graft agency, taken ten days to the gubernatorial election scheduled to be held this coming Saturday, had been greeted with howls of outrage. Although some stakeholders have also queried the presidential intervention on grounds that it raises questions about the independence of EFCC, the president said he was deeply embarrassed, arguing that the timing of the restriction was inappropriate.

This latest controversy has merely deepened the tensions ahead of this weekend’s election. The build-up has been characterised by large-scale violence, intimidation, blood-letting and thuggery. The state is heaving with cultists, many of whom are reportedly being exploited by some of the political actors. Indeed, in the past one year alone, political violence has claimed more than two dozen lives. “We have issues of cultism in Osun already,” admitted the Inspector General of Police, (IGP) Olatunde Disu. “It became easier for different parties to attack each other using the existing animosity in the state.” Some 13 local government areas out of the 30 have been marked down as high-risk due largely to recurring violence and killings.

The climate of violence in the state is aided by the paralysis of the local government system, and the challenge of a managing a relatively poor state for 15 months without statutory funds. The dispute over statutory allocations to the councils persists even after the Supreme Court’s intervention. But the Osun election is particularly important because it is the last off-cycle governorship election before the 2027 general election. For many, it will act as a litmus test to the preparedness of the electoral bodies, the political parties as well as the security agencies.

Meanwhile, 14 candidates are challenging the incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, who is running for a re-election on the platform of the Accord Party, having earlier defected from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). However, the contest has essentially been narrowed down to three contenders: The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, who had served as Commissioner for Finance under former Governors Rauf Aregbesola and Gboyega Oyetola, and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate, Najeem Salaam, a former Speaker in the state House of Assembly as well as the incumbent Adeleke. Interestingly, all three frontline candidates are from the Osun West Senatorial District.

Since an ‘end justifies the means’ approach to politics has over the years provided the incentive and motivation for power seekers to believe that all is fair and acceptable in electoral politics, the success or failure of Osun polls will depend largely on the capacity of the security agencies that must remain neutral throughout the entire process. We hope the redeployment from election duties of Police Commissioner Ibrahim Gotan will help in providing a level playing field for all parties and candidates. No less important also is the role of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as an impartial arbiter. Fortunately, INEC has had ample time to prepare and get its act together by ensuring that all logistical problems like late arrival of ballot papers and voting materials to polling centres are not repeated.

But the onus is still on the politicians in the state to give peace a chance. At the end, the choice of who governs Osun for the next four years is that of the residents of the state to make. May the best candidate win.

World.title: First HoldCo, Zenith Bank, GTCO, UBA, Eight Others’ Market Capitalisation Hits N27.4tn in July
World.content:
Kayode Tokede



Driven by strong corporate earnings and renewed investors’ appetite for banking stocks, the combined market capitalisation of Zenith Bank, Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO), First Bank (First HoldCo Plc), United Bank for Africa (UBA), Access Holdings Plc, Fidelity Bank, Wema Bank, and five other listed banks on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) rose to N27.4 trillion at the close of trading in July 2026, from N23.33 trillion at the end of June.

The N27.4 trillion valuation represented about 17.3 per cent of the NGX’s overall market capitalisation of N158.33 trillion as of July 31, 2026.



During the month under review, the NGX Banking Index appreciated by 22.10 per cent, outperforming the broader market and several other major sectoral indices.

On a year-to-date (YtD) basis, the Banking Index ranked among the leading sectoral indices on the Exchange, behind the NGX Oil & Gas and NGX Industrial Goods indices, which had appreciated by 96.32 per cent and 85.42 per cent respectively.

The NGX All-Share Index (ASI), meanwhile, gained 6.92 per cent in July, bringing its YtD return to 57.62 per cent, driven by sustained investors’ confidence, improved conditions in the foreign exchange market, impressive corporate earnings and renewed demand for fundamentally sound stocks.



First HoldCo emerged as the most capitalised banking stock on the NGX at the end of July, ahead of Zenith Bank Plc and Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO).

The market capitalisation of First HoldCo jumped from N2.55 trillion at the end of June to N5.88 trillion in July, following a spectacular rally in its share price.

The company’s share price appreciated by 131.13 per cent during the period, closing in July at N129.55 per share, up from N56.05 per share at the end of June.



The surge in the company’s share price followed further accumulation of its shares by its Chairman, Mr. Femi Otedola, as well as investors’ positive reaction to its impressive financial performance for the first half (H1) of 2026.

First HoldCo had announced its unaudited financial results for the half-year ended June 30, 2026, reporting profit before tax (PBT) of N653.5 billion, representing an increase of 83.5 per cent from N356.1 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

Profit after tax (PAT) similarly rose by 81.5 per cent to N526.1 billion in H1 2026, from N289.8 billion in H1 2025.



Zenith Bank and GTCO occupied the second and third positions, respectively, with market capitalisations of N5.07 trillion and N4.75 trillion at the end of July, compared with N4.52 trillion and N4.57 trillion, respectively, in June.

United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA) saw its market capitalisation rise to N1.97 trillion in July from N1.70 trillion in June, while Access Holdings Plc’s valuation increased to N1.43 trillion from N1.20 trillion during the same period.



Other listed financial institutions included Fidelity Bank Plc, with a market capitalisation of N1.36 trillion; Wema Bank Plc, N1.16 trillion; FCMB Group Plc, N755.18 billion; Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc, N527.43 billion; and Jaiz Bank Plc.

However, Ecobank Transnational Incorporated (ETI) and Stanbic IBTC Holdings Plc bucked the bullish trend, recording declines in their share prices during the month.



ETI’s share price declined by 6.56 per cent, while Stanbic IBTC fell by 2.5 per cent.

ETI’s market capitalisation stood at N1.61 trillion at the end of July, compared with N2.55 trillion in June, while Stanbic IBTC’s valuation declined to N2.53 trillion from N2.59 trillion.



Commenting on the performance, Vice President, Highcap Securities Limited, Mr. David Adonri, attributed the rally in the Banking Index to strong demand for First HoldCo shares and impressive earnings reported by other listed banks.

“The NGX Banking Index being the best-performing index in July 2026 has to do with First HoldCo and Mr. Femi Otedola’s rising stake. The billionaire investor’s position has continued to drive the banking stock and boost other investors’ confidence,” Adonri said.

World.title: Okpebholo, Ododo, Umahi, Oyetola Rally against Adeleke
World.content:
•Army warns troops against partisanship

•Arrests of Accord Party leaders question police neutrality

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

As the campaign for the August 15 governorship election in Osun State gathers fresh momentum, Governors Monday Okpebholo of Edo State, Ahmed Usman Ododo of Kogi State; Minister of Works, David Umahi; and the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, have urged the people of the state to reject Governor Ademola Adeleke and elect the governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji.

This is just as the General Officer Commanding (GOC), 2 Division of the Nigerian Army, Major General Auwalu Mahmuda, has directed troops deployed for the governorship election to remain professional, politically neutral and strictly adhere to the Code of Conduct guiding military participation in election security operations.

However, concerns have been raised about the alleged lack of neutrality of the police following the alleged arrests of leaders of Accord Party in the state on the orders of the state Police Commissioner, Ibrahim Gotan.

Meanwhile, Governor Adeleke has again charged Osun voters to defend their votes in the spirit of democracy and the national constitution.

Okpebholo and other APC leaders made appeal in Osogbo during the official flag-off of the construction of the Osogbo-Iwo-Ibadan Road and the reconstruction of the Gbongan-Osogbo Road, a major federal infrastructure project initiated by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration.

Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, Oyetola described the APC governorship candidate as a competent, experienced, and visionary leader capable of transforming the state through purposeful governance.

He said Oyebamiji possesses the administrative capacity, political experience, and developmental vision required to reposition the state and align it with the federal government’s renewed infrastructure drive.

According to him, the forthcoming governorship election presents an opportunity for the people of the state to reconnect the state with the centre of national development.

In his remarks, Minister of Works, Umahi, described Oyebamiji as “President Tinubu’s political son,” adding that an APC victory in the state would further strengthen developmental partnerships capable of delivering more roads, improved infrastructure, employment opportunities and economic growth.

Also addressing the gathering, APC National Secretary, Senator Ajibola Basiru, called on the electorate to vote massively for the APC, arguing that the achievements of the Tinubu administration in infrastructure development have already begun to manifest across different parts of the country.

In his remarks, Governor Okpebholo also canvassed support for the APC candidate, saying governance requires practical leadership, strategic planning and the ability to deliver meaningful development to the people.

Similarly, Governor Ododo encouraged the electorate to support the APC to consolidate President Tinubu’s developmental agenda.

Army Warns Troops against Partisanship

The GOC gave the warning while addressing officers and soldiers deployed to support election security operations at the Engineer Construction Command (ECC) in Ede, Osun State.

Mahmuda reminded the troops that their deployment was in line with the Nigerian Army’s constitutional responsibility to provide aid to civil authorities when necessary.

He explained that the operation, codenamed Operation SAFE CONDUCT, was designed to support the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), which remains the lead agency responsible for election security in Nigeria.

According to him, soldiers are expected to provide only outer-cordon security and should intervene strictly when requested to respond to security threats.

He warned the troops to stay away from polling units except where their intervention becomes necessary in line with operational directives.

The GOC said the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, expects all personnel participating in the operation to demonstrate discipline, professionalism and absolute neutrality throughout the electoral process.

He cautioned the troops against political partisanship, intimidation of voters or any conduct capable of undermining the credibility of the election.

Mahmuda stressed that the troops must conduct themselves in a manner that reflects the core values of the Nigerian Army, urging them to avoid harassing members of the public while carrying out their duties.

Arrests of Accord Party Leaders Question Police Neutrality

Meanwhile, concerns have been raised about the alleged lack of neutrality of the police following the arrests of leaders of the Accord Party in the state on the orders of the state Police Commissioner, Ibrahim Gotan.

The spokesman of the Imole Campaign Council working for the reelection of Governor Adeleke, Mr. Pelumi Olajengbesi, yesterday decried the arrests of the state Commissioner for Environment and Sanitation, Hon. Mayowa Adejoorin, and 60 Accord members across the state, including Ijesaland, by the Osun State Police Command.

He said the action was meant to silence Accord leaders and compromise the August 15 governorship election.

Speaking at a press conference in Osogbo, he called on the Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu, to urgently intervene in the situation in Osun State.

He also drew the attention of Nigerians, the international community and the leadership of the Nigerian Police Force to the disturbing and increasingly dangerous pattern of arrests, intimidation and incessant abduction of leaders and members of the Accord Party, particularly across Ijesaland.

According to him, “The latest victim of this alarming pattern is the state Commissioner for Environment and Sanitation, Hon Mayowa Adejoorin, a prominent native of Ikiyinwa in Obokun Local Government Area of the state. ”

Olajengbesi added that the manner of his arrest was particularly disturbing.

He said, “We consider what happened to Hon Adejoorin nothing short of a bandit-line abduction carried out under the cover of police authority.”

“For some time now, we have witnessed a disturbing pattern in which prominent Accord leaders and supporters in Ijesaland are picked up by the Police on allegations that are apparently motivated by sinister political calculations, kept away from their families, communities and campaign activities, and thereby removed from circulation at a critical period of the electoral process.”

In a separate statement issued and made available by the Chairman, Media and Publicity Sub-Committee of the council, Hon. Bamidele Sallam, the campaign council, specifically accused CP Gotan of defying the directive of the IG that all police officers should be non-partisan.

The campaign council alleged that since the arrival of the new police Commissioner in charge of the election, the substantive CP, Gotan, has been running a parallel police structure which he has deployed alongside APC thugs to molest Accord Party leaders.

Defend Your Votes, Adeleke Charges Residents

Meanwhile, Governor Adeleke has again charged Osun voters to vote and defend their votes in the spirit of democracy and the national constitution.

He gave the admonition at the palaces of monarchs of Ipetu-Ijesha and Ijebu Ijesha as he rallied support for re-election alongside his cousin, David Adeleke a.k.a Davido, at a massively attended rally at Ijebujesha.

Accompanied by top leaders of the Imole Campaign Council, the governor tasked Osun voters to demonstrate boldness and determination to exercise their voting rights as guaranteed by the constitution, declaring that “no force can deny Osun voters their democratic rights”

Re-echoing Davido, who also challenged Osun residents to vote and defend their votes, the governor said free and fair elections are the inalienable rights of Osun people and “they are ready to protect and affirm those rights on August 15th.”

At the palace of Ajalaye of Ipetujesa, Oba Adeleke Oke, the monarch eulogised the governor for his extraordinary performance in the last four years, assuring the Accord team of total support of his people on August 15.

The royal father of Ijebu-Jesa, while welcoming the governor, hosted a victory prayer session in which interfaith activities in support of Accord’s triumph over opposition forces were held.

“You will win the second term, and you will deliver even more than you have done in your first term. My people are eager to continue to be part of a good turn of events in the state,” the royal father submitted.

At electrifying campaign rallies in Ipetu-Ijesha and Ijebu-Jesa, Governor Adeleke declared that victory was at hand and urged the people to intensify mobilisation for continuity.

“Your security is assured. Your safety is guaranteed. Mobilise your relatives and friends. Vote for good governance and more dividends of democracy.

“Ijesa people, Osun people cannot be scared. We are people of courage. Vote and defend your votes,” the governor told a mammoth crowd of supporters at both Ipetu-Ijesha and Ijebu-Jesa.

Police Confirms Arrest of Osun Commissioner

The Osun State Police Command yesterday confirmed the arrest of Osun State Commissioner for Environment, Mr. Mayowa Adejoorin over a shooting incident.

Speaking to journalists through its spokesperson, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, it said the commissioner was arrested in connection with the disruption of a political rally in Ilesa.

He stressed: “Immediately the incident was reported, our personnel moved to the scene, cordoned off the area before some exhibits were recovered which included expanded cartridges, Amotekun personnel caps.

“Also, Adejoorin was arrested at the scene and has been taken to the command for questioning as part of the investigation process,” he added.

World.title: St Stithians honours Cameron Waldeck-Cooks in Women’s Day message
World.content:
St Stithians College has paid tribute to late Grade 11 learner Cameron Waldeck-Cooks on Women’s Day, Sunday, 9 August. Image: ChatGPT

St Stithians College has paid tribute to late Grade 11 learner Cameron Waldeck-Cooks on Women’s Day, saying its community remains in “profound mourning” following her death.

marking Women’s Day on Sunday, the school said its thoughts were particularly with Cameron’s family as South Africa honoured the women and young women who contribute to their communities.

READ | St Stithians murder: Brother makes explosive allegation



“Our College remains in profound mourning following the tragic loss of Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, a deeply loved young woman in our Saints family,” the school said.

Honour the courage of women

The tribute comes as South Africa marks 70 years since the historic Women’s March of 1956, when more than 20 000 women marched to the Union Buildings in Pretoria to protest against the extension of pass laws to women.

St Stithians said the anniversary provided an opportunity to honour the courage of those women and recognise the progress made through their actions and the work of subsequent generations.

The school also acknowledged that significant challenges remain in the pursuit of equality, dignity and justice.

“As a St Stithians community, we reaffirm our commitment to continuing that work,” the college said.

Murder investigation

Cameron, 17, was found dead at a lodge in Sabie, Mpumalanga, earlier this month alongside St Stithians alumnus Ethan Coetzee, 19.



Police have since opened a murder investigation following post-mortem findings which suggested Cameron may have been strangled.

Police believe Coetzee died by suicide.

RELATED | Where did Cameron and Ethan die? Sabie, the quiet town at the centre of a murder investigation

Cameron’s parents, Derrick Cooks and Claire Waldeck-Cooks, have urged the public not to speculate about the circumstances surrounding their daughter’s death while the investigation and forensic processes continue.

The family has also asked for privacy as they mourn her loss.

A memorial service is expected to be held later in August.

World.title: ‘No sign of altercation’: Ethan Coetzee’s family breaks silence
World.content:
Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee died at the Waterval self-catering lodge in Mpumalanga. Images via Airbnb/ St Stithians

The family of Ethan Coetzee have broken their silence, disputing preliminary findings that he was involved in the death of his girlfriend, St Stithians Grade 11 learner Cameron Waldeck-Cooks.

The former matriculant is believed to have died by suicide, whilst Cameron was allegedly strangled to death. Their bodies were found in a Sabie game lodge on Monday, 3 August, by Ethan’s father.

The teenage couple had enjoyed a hiking expedition at the game reserve alongside family members.



ETHAN COETZEE’S FAMILY BREAKS SILENCE

In a statement, the family of Ethan Coetzee, a St Stithians alumnus, disputed that he was involved in the alleged murder of his girlfriend, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks.

The family claimed that there was “no sign of an altercation” and that Ethan “sustained no injuries consistent with a struggle”.

They added that the couple appeared happy the night before their deaths.

Ethan was described as “kind, gentle and loyal”, particularly towards Cameron.

Their bodies were described inside the Waterval Self-Catering Holiday Home by Ethan’s father, Graham Coetzee.

‘MURDER’ SAYS CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS’ BROTHER

While Ethan Coetzee’s family have disputed allegations he was involved in Cameron Waldeck-Cooks’s death, the late teen’s brother, also Ethan, accused her partner of “murder”,

In a screenshot of an Instagram post, Ethan shared:

“My sister, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, was found dead…Her corpse lay lifeless, with injuries in several parts of her body. She was murdered by Ethan Coetzee. There was no drug overdose, no poison, no suicide pact. Ethan Coetzee suffocated my sister to death by strangulation. She did not pass peacefully.

He continued: “And while both passings affect many lives in diverse ways, I will not sit by myself and watch as people celebrate my sister’s murderer. He was a brother to me, he always treated me with kindness and respect, and he enlightened my family. But to me, all his virtuous deeds mean nothing now.

“My sister was only 17 years old and had her life taken away from her. I know my sister and what she stands for. And that is to speak up”



Ethan added that he was infuriated about posts and tributes to Ethan Coetzee, particularly those that included images of the late teens together.

He added: “The trauma he caused her and my family will not be forgotten”

WHAT WE DO KNOW

Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, 17, and Ethan Coetzee, 19, were found dead at a lodge in the Sabie area of Mpumalanga on Monday, 3 August. Cameron was a Grade 11 learner at St Stithians Girls College, while Ethan had matriculated in 2025.

Police initially investigated the deaths as an inquest, and initially suspected that no foul play was involved.

However, post-mortem findings changed the direction of the investigation.

According to preliminary findings as well as the opinion of an independent forensic pathologist involved, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks died from strangulation/suffocation.

Ethan’s death is believed to be a suicide.

Police have subsequently opened a murder case in connection with Cameron’s death.

No person has been charged with Cameron’s murder, and police have not publicly announced that Ethan was legally determined to be her killer. The investigation continues.

World.title: Update: Safa double Pitso Mosimane’s salary offer to R10 million-a-year
World.content:
The South African Football Association (SAFA) have approved Mosimane’s appointment as the successor to Hugo Broos. Negotiations now focus on finalising his contract and salary.

According to SABC Sport, SAFA initially offered Mosimane a package worth R5 million per year. It was communicated to him by CFO Grony Hluyo following a meeting between the association’s senior executives and the former Mamelodi Sundowns and Al Ahly coach.

The initial offer was significantly below the reported R1.4 million-a-month salary Broos earned during his time in charge of Bafana Bafana.



However, SAFA have now reportedly doubled that initial package following Saturday’s National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting at SAFA House, which approved Mosimane’s return.

PITSO MOSIMANE’S SAFA RETURN

The SAFA Technical Committee, led by Jack Maluleke, had already identified Mosimane as their preferred candidate to replace Broos.

SAFA’s senior executives subsequently visited Mosimane as they worked towards finalising his return to the national team. The delegation included CEO Lydia Monyepao, CFO Grony Hluyo, Technical Director Molefi Ntseki and Chief Medical Officer Thulani Ngwenya.

The latest development suggests SAFA are prepared to make a significantly bigger financial commitment.

Mosimane began his professional head coaching career with SuperSport United in 2001.

His six-year spell included consecutive second-place finishes in the Premier Soccer League, while he also won several domestic cup trophies.



His success earned him an opportunity with Bafana Bafana. First as caretaker coach in 2007. He later worked as an assistant under Carlos Alberto Parreira and Joel Santana during the build-up to the 2010 FIFA World Cup.

In July 2010, Mosimane was promoted to permanent head coach. He started his reign with a 1-0 victory over Ghana. But his first spell with Bafana Bafana ended in disappointment in 2012.

A mathematical error surrounding the qualification permutations after a draw against Sierra Leone resulted in South Africa missing out on the 2012 Africa Cup of Nations. Mosimane was subsequently dismissed.

BAFANA BAFANA LEGACY

Mosimane’s reputation grew considerably after his first Bafana Bafana spell. He joined Mamelodi Sundowns in late 2012. He embarked on an eight-year golden era that transformed the club into one of Africa’s dominant forces.

Mosimane won five domestic league titles with Sundowns. He also delivered the club’s greatest continental achievement in 2016. He won the CAF Champions League.

That triumph made Mosimane the first South African coach to lead a South African club to the continental crown. His success earned him a move to Egyptian giants Al Ahly in 2020.

He guided the Cairo giants to consecutive CAF Champions League titles in 2020 and 2021. He also led Al Ahly to two bronze medals at the FIFA Club World Cup

Mosimane later expanded his international coaching experience with spells at Saudi Arabian clubs Al-Ahli Jeddah and Abha Club, UAE side Al Wahda and Iranian giants Esteghlal.

Now, in August 2026, Mosimane is set to return to the Bafana Bafana hot seat. SAFA’s decision to double the initial offer underlines the importance attached to his appointment.

His challenge will be to turn that momentum into sustained success and build a Bafana Bafana side capable of competing consistently at the highest level of African football.

South Africa faces a high-stakes shootout in Group D of the AFCON 2027 qualifiers against Guinea, Eritrea, and co-hosts Kenya. Because Kenya automatically qualifies as hosts, only one other team from this group can advance to the finals. This unique rule eliminates the safety net of a second-place finish, meaning Bafana Bafana must essentially outperform Guinea to secure their spot.

The entire campaign takes place over three quick international windows, starting with Matchdays 1 and 2 in September 2026. South Africa opens at home against Guinea before traveling to Eritrea. They will face Kenya in a November 2026 double-header, and then wrap up the final group matches in March 2027 to decide who books their ticket to East Africa.
